New York Distilling Co. Perry’s Tot

name: Eastside
description: The Eastside is a gin-based cocktail recipe from New York City, New York.
instructions:
1. Add three cucumbers slices and mint leaves to a shaker.
2. Muddle gently for 5-7 seconds.
3. Add gin, lime juice, simple syrup, and cubed ice to shaker.
4. Shake for 10-20 seconds.
5. Fine strain into a cocktail glass.
garnish: Garnish with remaining cucumber slice and mint sprig.

name: Eeyore’s Requiem
description: Three bitter amari, including Fernet-Branca, get amped up with aromatic French vermouth and juniper-rich gin in this cocktail recipe.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Express three orange twists over the surface of the drink, discarding the first two and saving the third for garnish.

name: Eggnog
description: An archetypal example of a traditional eggnog recipe with farm-fresh dairy and a blend of whiskey, rum and Cognac.
instructions:
1. Separate the eggs.
2. Whisk the yolks and sugar together until they firm up and their bright orange color fades to a more opaque pale yellow.
3. Slowly add the spirits, milk and cream while continuing to whisk air into the batch.
4. Beat the egg whites and salt together to stiff peaks.
5. Whisk the egg whites into the mixture.
6. Bottle and store in the refrigerator until chilled, the longer the better.
7. When ready to serve, pour into a chilled Nick & Nora glass and top with freshly grated nutmeg.

name: El Abuelo
description: This Old Fashioned-inspired cocktail adds warmth and depth to the whiskey cocktail using the earthy herbaceousness of a Mexican amaro and the baking spices of a spiced brown nectar.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir for approximately 10 seconds.
2. Strain over a large ice cube into the glass.
3. Garnish.
garnish: Sprig of thyme and an orange swath

lines.note: such as Maxico Mistico Licor del Sobador

name: El Gibson
description: This Gibson riff uses the brine of pickled spring onions as the dirty. If spring onions aren’t in season, the recipe still works perfectly well using small yellow onions.
instructions:
1. Place the pickled onion wedge in a chilled Nick & Nora glass. In a mixing glass, stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into the prepared glass.
2. Pickled Spring OnionsThoroughly wash a bunch of spring onions, and use a knife to remove all of the green parts. Cut the onions into wedges, maintaining the root end (to hold the onion together). Pack the onions into a sanitized canning jar or a large food-safe plastic storage container.
3. In a pot, combine a mixture of 60 percent water and 40 percent champagne vinegar (the quantity will depend on the size of the batch you’re preparing). Weigh this liquid mixture and add 5 percent of its weight in sugar, and 3 percent of its weight in salt. Add several bay leaves, 1 Tbsp. of black peppercorns, and 1 Tbsp. of coriander seeds, and bring the mixture to a boil, whisking to dissolve the sugar.
4. Once the mixture is boiling, remove it from the heat and pour it over the onions, to cover. Cover the container and let it cool; will keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.

name: El Pepe
description: Although the El Pepe cocktail recipe looks innocent in a glass, it’s delightfully complex, built with a structure similar to Margarita.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over a large rock into a rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a basil leaf.

name: El Presidente
description: The El Presidente earned its acclaim in Havana during the 1920s through the 1940s during the American Prohibition. It quickly became the preferred drink of the Cuban upper class.
instructions: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.

name: Elder Fashion (Gin)
instructions: Stir everything with ice, strain to glass.

name: Electric Current Fizz
description: The Electric Current Fizz is an easy cocktail recipe that pairs a gin fizz with a prairie oyster, a dressed egg yolk shot.
instructions:
1. In a shaker, combine all ingredients except for soda water. Add one small piece of ice and shake until the ice is dissolved; this helps emulsify the egg white.
2. Add more ice to the shaker and hard shake, then strain into a fizz glass or short Collins glass.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Serve the fizz with the prairie oyster in a shot glass.

### Prairie Oyster

Reserve the egg yolk, taking care not to puncture it. Season the yolk with a pinch of salt, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco to taste (start with one dash of each). Serve in a shot glass alongside the drink.


Note: The appeal of the Prairie Oyster lies in the seasoned yolk bursting during the shot, so take care not to puncture it.
garnish: Prairie Oyster in a shot glass

name: Endless Summer
description: This riff on the Negroni cocktail recipe uses Campari, gin, sweet vermouth, and an ounce of pineapple.
instructions:
1. In a large shaking tin, add all ingredients. Add ice, and shake well.
2. Fine strain into a Collins glass over ice.


 ## Editors note:

This drink can easily be scaled up into a large-format cocktail.

name: English Garden
description: The English Garden brings together some classic pairings for St-Germain Elderflower liqueur - gin, apple, lime & cucumber. Served long, this one is filled with quintessential English flavours.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain over fresh ice into a high ball

name: Enzo
description: The Enzo is an Americano cocktail made with a Ferrari, the 50/50 shot of fernet amaro and Campari. Here’s the easy aperitivo recipe.
instructions:
1. Add the first three ingredients to a Collins or highball glass over ice.
2. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange peel or a half-slice.

name: Enzoni
description: The Enzoni Cocktail is a true modern classic that will impress your guests! This gin-based drink is perfect for any occasion and is a fun and delicious take on some of your favorite classic cocktails!
instructions: Muddle grapes, add ingredients, shake then double strain. Garnish with more green grapes on a cocktail pick.

name: Eponine Collins
description: A French-inflected Collins cocktail recipe builds on a base of gin, complemented by Suze and Amaro Montenegro.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a collins glass over ice and top with soda.
3. Garnish with two cucumber slices and two basil leaves.

name: Espresso Irish Coffee
description: The best Irish Coffee cocktail recipe, which won our tasting of variations on the drink, combines Irish whiskey, espresso and whipped cream.
instructions:
1. Add the whiskey and simple syrup into a mixing tin.
2. Add a small amount of boiling water to an 11-ounce mug to heat it, and nestle the tin in the mug so that the tin heats as well.
3. Dump the water out of the mug, add the whiskey-sugar mixture and top with boiling water to about 1 inch below the rim of the glass.
4. Pour the espresso shot directly into the mug.
5. Float the cream on top and garnish with freshly grated cinnamon.


 ## Editors note:

### Whipped Heavy Cream:

Pour several ounces of heavy cream into a mixing tin. Dry shake without ice until the cream begins to thicken, but is still pourable.

lines.note: preferably Powers Gold Label Irish Whiskey

name: Espresso Martini
description: It is not a true martini as it contains neither gin nor vermouth, but is one of many drinks that incorporate the term martini into their names.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.

name: Fairy Sugar Momma
description: As much as I liked the hint of anise in a corpse reviver I never was one to eat a black jelly bean on its own. But I think this drink works so well because all of the ingredients it’s brought together with are also bold and don't allow the absinthe to dominate the drink. It’s black jelly bean on a tropical vacation and it is tasty.
instructions: Shake ingredients

name: Fancy Free
description: The Fancy Free is a variation on the Old-Fashioned. This cocktail recipe combines bourbon whiskey, maraschino liqueur and bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled double rocks glass over a big cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

lines.note: preferably Elijah Craig Small Batch or Old Forester

name: Femme Fatale
description: Rather than serving sparkling wine alongside this Pornstar Martini variation, it is added directly to the glass. A vanilla infusion lends to a drier finish than the traditional addition of vanilla-flavored liqueur, with the passion fruit providing a citrusy, floral, and melon-forward brightness highlighted by the toasty cremant.
instructions:
1. Pour the sparkling wine into a chilled coupe. Shake the remaining ingredients and fine strain into the coupe. Optional: Shake hibiscus dust on the surface of the cocktail and swirl with a barspoon.
Passion Fruit Vanilla SyrupIf using frozen purée, thaw 2 1/4 oz. of passion fruit purée (such as Perfect Purée) completely and bring to room temperature. Add 2 1/4 oz. of granulated sugar and 1/3 tsp. of vanilla syrup and whisk to combine completely. Refrigerate to store. Makes approximately 6 servings and will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Hibiscus DustUsing a spice grinder, pulse 1/4 cup of dried hibiscus flowers to a fine powder. Store in a shaker. Makes approximately 6 servings.

name: Fernandito
description:
The cocktail first became popular among the youth of the college town of Córdoba, in the 1980s and—impulsed by an advertising campaign led by Fratelli Branca—its consumption grew in popularity during the following decades to become widespread throughout the country, surpassed only by that of beer and wine. It is now considered a cultural icon of Argentina and is especially associated with its home province of Córdoba, where the drink is most consumed. The popularity of fernet con coca is such that Argentina consumes more than 75% of all fernet produced globally. The cocktail can also be found in some of its bordering countries, like Uruguay.

Although typically made with Fernet-Branca and Coca-Cola, several amaro brands have appeared in Argentina since its popularization, as well as ready-to-drink versions.
instructions: Pour the Fernet Branca into a double old fashioned glass with ice, fill the glass up with Cola. Gently stir.

name: Ferrari
description: The Ferrari cocktail recipe, a potent 50/50 split of Fernet-Branca and Campari, can be taken as a shot or sipped slowly.
instructions: 1. Combine and drink as a shot.

name: Final Ward
description:
The Final Ward is perhaps the best-know riff on the classic Last Word and was created in 2007 in NYC. It is still comprised of equal parts with rye whiskey replacing the gin and fresh lemon juice in place of lime.

The Last Word is a gin-based prohibition-era cocktail which was rediscovered in 2004 and becoming a cult hit in the Seattle area.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
garnish: Cocktail cherry at the bottom of the glass

name: Fiore di Francia
description: In this cocktail recipe Italian amaro, Cynar, joins forces with St-Germain in a nod to the border zone where elderflower grows freely.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing glass, add ice and stir.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express the lemon peel and discard.

name: First Frost
description: Even though carrots are available year round, this drink celebrates how the veggie can lend an earthy warmth and a natural sweetness to cocktails. It layers the flavors with the slow heat of a homemade honey syrup infused with cloves and jalapeños.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously until well chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish.

name: Five Point Palm Exploding Heart Technique
description: This smoky, bittersweet cocktail combines mezcal’s earthy intensity with the bitter depth of Punt e Mes and the richness of coffee liqueur. Chocolate bitters tie everything together with a roasty, slightly bitter finish. A brooding, complex drink with martial-arts-level impact—sip slowly and with respect.
instructions:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the ingredients
2. Stir until chilled
3. Strain over ice into a rocks glass

name: Flannel Shirt
description: The Flannel Shirt was created for an autumnal event. Using classic fall flavors—apple, earth, spice and smoke—it is a fleecy, bone-warming drink with the bold backbone of Scotch and a supporting cast of apple cider, St. Elizabeth Allspice Dram and super-bold Averna.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.

name: Floppydisk
description: The tricky thing when it comes to low ABV drinks is that the end result doesn’t always give that same feeling of a proper mixed drink. They can easily lack complexity and fall flat. This drink is half the booze and double the flavor.
instructions: Shake without soda

name: Floradora
description: A little spice and a burst of berry flavor - this highball is perfect for a sunny afternoon.
instructions:
1. Short shake all ingredients except soda water
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice
3. Top with soda water and stir.

name: For Mezcalicus Sake
instructions:
1. Stir all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into chilled glass.
garnish: Express lime zest twist over cocktail and use as garnish.

name: Four Points
description: A very tropical Last Word. Bright, funky and perfectly balanced.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe

name: French 75
description: The drink dates to World War I, and an early form was created in 1915 in Paris. The combination was said to have such a kick that it felt like being shelled with the powerful French 75mm field gun.
instructions:
1. Pour all the ingredients, except Champagne, into a shaker.
2. Shake well and strain into a Champagne flute.
3. Top up with Champagne.
4. Stir gently.

name: French Connection
description: The cocktail is named for the Gene Hackman film of the same name.
instructions: Pour all ingredients directly into an old fashioned glass filled with ice cubes. Stir gently.

name: French Gimlet
description: A simple 3-ingredient riff on a classic Gimlet. St-Germain Elderflower Liqueur is used as the sweetener to balance the tart lime juice. The French Gimlet highlights the bright, citrusy and floral notes of St Germain.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass

name: French Martini
description:
It was invented in the 1980s in New York City. The cocktail was produced during the 1980s–1990s cocktail renaissance.

It is not a true martini, but is one of many drinks that incorporate the term martini into their names. The key ingredient that makes a martini "French" is Chambord, a black raspberry liqueur that has been produced in France since 1685.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.
garnish: Squeeze oil from lemon peel onto the drink.

name: French Pearl
description: This cocktail recipe puts gin and pastis in the same shaken drink—along with lime juice, simple syrup and mint leaves.
instructions:
1. In a shaker tin, add the lime juice, simple syrup and mint then muddle.
2. Add the gin, pastis and ice and shake until chilled.
3. Fine strain into a coupe.

name: French Pearl
description: This refreshing, elegant libation is a tribute to the Beaux-Arts Neoclassical architectural movement of the late 1800s in France, an era in which sipping pastis was quite fashionable. The “pearl” refers to the visual opacity of the drink, an effect referred to as “louching,” which naturally occurs when any anise-flavored liqueur or spirit meets water.
instructions:
1. Combine the lime juice, cane syrup, and mint sprig in a cocktail shaker.
2. Muddle the ingredients.
3. Next, add the Pernod and gin.
4. Fill the shaker to the top with ice and shake well.
5. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Fresh Grapefruit Paloma
description: Coming in on top in our Paloma tasting was this cocktail, using El Tesoro Blanco tequila.
instructions:
1. Salt the rim of the Collins glass, then add the Topo Chico and set aside.
2. Combine all the remaining ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the Collins glass, add ice, and garnish with a lime wedge.

name: Frozen Margarita
description: A frozen Margarita cocktail recipe made with tequila, Cointreau, fresh lime and orange juices and raw agave.
instructions:
1. Prepare the glass, if using the lime-salt rim. Moisten half the rim of a double rocks glass with a lime wheel, then dip gently in kosher salt.
2. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
3. Fill a 13-ounce double rocks glass with a heaping scoop of pebble ice (see Editor’s Note).
4. Add ice to the blender and blend until smooth.
5. Pour into a double rocks glass.
garnish: lime and kosher salt rim, optional

name: Frozen Mudslide
description: This reworks the 1980s mudslide. Incorporating ice cream into the mudslide removes the need for ice resulting in a richer flavour.
instructions:
1. In a blender jug, combine all the ingredients
2. Blend until smooth
3. Served in a tall glass

name: Fumata Bianca
description: This cocktail recipe is a soft, yet edgy mixture of sweet blanca vermouth, herbal Suze, and smoky mezcal that goes down easy.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the grapefruit twist in a collins glass.
2. Add ice and top with club soda.
3. Express a grapefruit twist over the drink and drop into the glass.

name: Garibaldi
description: This drink is named after Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi, who was a central figure in the unification of Italy. Its two ingredients—Campari from the north acting as a nod to the red shirts worn by Garibaldi’s freedom fighters and bright orange representing Sicily to the south—are symbolic of its heritage.
instructions:
1. Build the Campari and orange juice in a small highball glass filled with ice.
2. Stir and garnish with the orange wedge.

name: Garibaldi Spritz
description: This version of the classic Garibaldi cocktail recipe dials back the Campari and tops all with prosecco, turning the classic into a spritz.
instructions:
1. To an ice-filled Collins glass, add the Campari and orange juice and stir to combine.
2. Top with prosecco and garnish.

name: Gemišt
description: Coming from a german word "gemischt", meaning mixed. Popular in Balkan countries, especially with homemade dry white wines.
instructions:
Combine cold ingredients in a glass.
Ingredient amounts are usually eyeballed depending on the glass.

name: Gentleman’s Exchange
description: A strong rocks cocktail with an emphasis on coffee and bourbon
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients except the grapefruit peel in a mixing glass and stir for about ten seconds
2. Pour into a rocks glass over a large cube and garnish with the grapefruit peel

name: Getaway Car
description: This take on the Jungle Bird cocktail recipe swaps in Ancho Reyes for Campari—alongside a kick of ancho chili powder.
instructions:
1. Fill a shaker tin half-full with pebble ice.
2. Add all ingredients and shake.
3. Fill a Zombie mug half-full with pebble ice.
4. Strain into the mug, and garnish with a lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder.
garnish: lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder

name: Ghost Coast
description: An unforgettable tour of western America in cocktail form
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice and garnish
garnish: eucalyptus leaf and/or banana chip for garnish

name: Gibson
description: More fun than answering who first plopped a pickled pearl onion—instead of an olive, or a lemon twist—into a dry gin Martini is recalling who didn’t. The drink’s origins have yet to be cracked, although the urban sophistication of a Martini paired with a pickled twist has left largely anyone with the last name Gibson receiving credit for the drink. Most perplexing of all, the earliest renditions of the Gibson, such as one from 1908, make no mention of an onion. As for the unsolved onion, some veggie tales are best left to the imagination.
instructions:
1. Stir the ingredients with ice to chill, then strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
2. Garnish with the pickled pearl onion.

name: Gimlet
description: The word "gimlet" used in this sense is first attested in 1928. The most obvious derivation is from the tool for drilling small holes, a word also used figuratively to describe something as sharp or piercing. Thus, the cocktail may have been named for its "penetrating" effects on the drinker.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lime juice, and syrup to a cocktail shaker. Fill with ice and shake until cold.
2. Strain into glass and top with a splash of soda water, if desired.

name: Gin Basil Smash
description: The drink was created in 2008. It is served at bars all across Germany.
instructions:
1. Muddle basil leaves in a shaker tin.
2. Add remaining ingredients and ice and shake until chilled.
3. Double strain into a rocks glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with basil leaves.

name: Gin Blossom
description: The Gin Blossom is a modern play on the classic Martini cocktail recipe.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice, and stir to chill.
3. Strain into a coupe glass and garnish with an expressed orange peel.

name: Gin Daisy (New School)
description: This cocktail recipe is a variation on the basic Daisy formula: a sour kicked up with the addition of seltzer or soda water.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, grenadine and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Garnish with a slice of orange.

name: Gin Fizz
description: A gin fizz is the best-known cocktail in the fizz family. The drink is similar to a Tom Collins, with a possible distinction being a Tom Collins historically used "Old Tom Gin" (a slightly sweeter precursor to London Dry Gin), whereas the kind of gin historically used in a gin fizz is unknown.
instructions:
1. Shake all ingredients with ice except soda water.
2. Pour into thin tall Tumbler glass
3. Top with a splash soda water
4. Serve without ice
garnish: Garnish with a lemon slice, optional lemon zest.

name: Gin-Gin Mule
description: This cocktail recipe is essentially a Mojito (a rum drink) crossed with a Moscow Mule (a vodka drink), but made with gin.
instructions:
1. Combine the lime juice, syrup and mint in a mixing glass and muddle.
2. Add the gin and ginger beer and ice and shake well.
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with mint leaves

name: Gin & It
description: The Gin & It is a classic cocktail recipe made with London dry gin, sweet vermouth, Angostura bitters. Here's how to make it.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain into a glass on the rocks.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Gin Pahit
description: An easy cocktail recipe from Malaysia. The classic drink combines gin, bitters and absinthe, but this simply version forgoes the latter.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Nick & Nora glass, then garnish with the lemon twist on the rim of the glass.

name: Gin Rickey
description: A juicy, aromatic Gin Rickey cocktail recipe created for a Mediterranean restaurant.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a highball glass over ice.
3. Top with club soda.
4. Garnish with straw, lemon and lime ribbons and fresh basil.
garnish: straw, lemon and lime ribbons, fresh basil

name: Gin & Tonic
description: Called a “G and T” or gin tonic in some countries, this refreshing drink is made in countries all around the world. The Gin and Tonic was invented in the 1850’s by British soldiers, who mixed gin with their tonic water as a way to drink quinine (which was thought to cure malaria). Tonic water of today no longer has quinine, but the drink stuck around!
instructions:
1. Add lots of ice to a large cocktail or wine glass and stir to chill the glass. Drain any melted water.
2. Pour in the gin. Add the garnishes. Pour the tonic water onto a bar spoon into the glass (to increase the bubbles). Stir once and serve.
garnish: Any of the following to spice your cocktail: Lime, lemon, cucumber, mint, orange peel, juniper berries, blood orange slice, rosemary

name: Gin & Tonic with Julienned Lime
description: The best Gin and Tonic cocktail recipe, which won our blind tasting of the drink, combines Tanqueray gin, tonic water and julienned lime.
instructions:
1. Clean well a fat, fresh lime. Cut in half and juice both halves, setting the juice aside for another use. Julienne the spent hulls into thin strips and put into a small mixing tin or glass. Add gin and muddle well for a minute or so.
2. In a large highball glass half-filled with ice, pour the tonic water carefully at a slant, so as to not disturb the effervescence, and slip a straw down the side of the glass now.
3. Strain the gin-lime mixture over a spoon onto the top, so that it floats. With tongs or a spoon, garnish atop with the julienned strips of lime. Present as such, but mix lightly before drinking.


 ## Editors note:

This may seem a stiff pour, but in maceration the juiced hulls will actually soak up a significant cut of the gin—up to 3/4 ounce—and can leave the drink wan if not fortified a touch.

name: Giving Basil
description: This drink takes the classic Gimlet, adds an herbaceous complexity with Italicus liqueur and basil, then rounds out the flavors and texture with pistachio orgeat for an irresistibly smooth sipper.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake, then double strain into a chilled glass.
3. Spritz with the vanilla tincture, then garnish.
garnish: Small basil leaf or dried basil blossom

name: Go-To
description: A guest once responded to this drink with "Oh, so it's your go-to?" inspiring the cocktail's name.
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients except the ginger beer
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a highball glass
4. Top with ginger beer
garnish: Garnish with a mint sprig and cucumber wheels

name: Godfather
description: The Godfather cocktail is a simple Scotch and amaretto drink that’s full of flavor! It pairs nutty sweetness with a spicy whiskey finish.
instructions:
1. Add the blended scotch and amaretto to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain the drink into a lowball glass and fill it with ice. (To take it over the top, add a splash of single malt scotch on top).

name: Godfather IV
description: A riff on the amaretto-sweetened Godfather cocktail recipe, this drink adds on walnut liqueur for extra depth and nutty richness.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Going Out West
description: This smoky sipper is the perfect Wild West-ish twist on the Old Fashioned, featuring rye whiskey, mezcal for a touch of smoke, and Averna amaro for depth.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, mezcal, amaro, and simple syrup to a mixing glass.
2. Add a good amount of ice and string for 20-30 seconds.
3. Strain into an old fashioned glass with a large cube.
4. Get an orange peel, squeeze it to express oils, and throw the garnish into the glass.

name: Gold Rush
description: Created in New York City in the early 2000s, this drink's combination of bourbon, lemon and honey became worldwide modern classic.
instructions:
1. Add the bourbon, honey syrup, and lemon juice into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over one large ice cube.

name: Golden Dream
description:
The Golden Dream was popular during the 60s and 70s and originated in Miami.

The cocktail was dedicated to actress Joan Crawford and became quite popular at the end of the 1960s on the east coast of the United States.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into shaker filled with ice. Shake briskly for few seconds. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

name: Good Christian Pear
instructions:
1. Shake with ice
2. Double-strain into a coupe.
garnish: Garnish with a pear slice or lemon wheel.

name: Gram-Arita
description: A Cadillac Margarita made with reposado tequila, Grand Marnier and lime juice.
instructions:
1. Rim half of a glass with salt and set aside.
2. Combine first three ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
4. Float Grand Marnier on top.

name: Grand Collins
description: A riff on a Tom Collins, the Grand Collins playfully swaps out Old Tom Gin for Grand Marnier, creating an intriguing, layered flavour profile to match its lively effervescence.
instructions: Place ice cubes in a highball glass and add Grand Marnier®, and then fresh lemon juice. Top up with soda water and stir.

name: Grapefruit Mai Tai
description: The Grapefruit Mai Tai is a tiki cocktail recipe. The tropical drink combines rum, absinthe, grapefruit and more.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Dump into a double rocks glass and top with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry, lime wedge and mint bouquet.
garnish: brandied cherry, lime wedge, fresh mint

lines.note: preferably John D Taylor's Velvet Falernum

name: Grapefruit Reviver
description: For this take on the Brown Derby, this drink leans into its grapefruit flavor with Malört. High-proof whiskey and rich demerara syrup help balance the strong, bitter notes, while creating a bourbon cocktail with depth.
instructions: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake to chill. Strain into the glass. Garnish.

name: Grasshopper
description: A Grasshopper is a sweet, mint-flavored, after-dinner drink. The name of the drink derives from its green color, which comes from crème de menthe. The drink is claimed to have been invented in 1918 in the French Quarter of New Orleans, Louisiana. The drink gained popularity during the 1950s and 1960s throughout the American South.
instructions:
1. Pour all ingredients into shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake briskly for few seconds.
3. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

name: Grasshopper Blanco
description: This twist on the Grasshopper uses blanco tequila to help cut through the drink's sweetness.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker.
2. Add ice and hard shake to incorporate the cream and chill.
3. Double strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.

name: Green Eyes
description: Chartreuse ups the herbacousness of this gin cocktail.
instructions:
1. Dry-shake all ingredients without ice to combine, then add ice and shake again until chilled and foamy.
2. Double-strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice; garnish.

name: Greta Garbo
description: A Daiquiri cocktail riff adding a few dashes of absinthe to the classic mix of white rum, lime juice and sugar.
instructions: 1. Shake all ingredients with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into a 5 1/2-ounce coupe glass.

name: Grog
description:
For over 300 years, the British Navy issued a daily 'tot' of rum, sometimes with double issues before battle. In 1740, as an attempt to combat drunkenness, a British admiral gave orders that the standard daily issue of half a pint of neat, high-proof rum be replaced with two servings of a quarter of a pint, diluted 4:1 with water. The Admiral was nicknamed 'Old Grogram' due to the waterproof grogram cloak he wore, so the mixture he introduced became known as 'grog'. Lime juice was often added to the grog in an attempt to prevent scurvy, lending British sailors their 'limey' nickname.

The 'tot' tradition, which was started by the British Navy in Jamaica in 1665, was finally broken on 31st July 1970, a day known as Black Tot Day, although by then, the 'tot' had been reduced to a meagre two ounces.

I hate to let the truth ruin a good story, but historians now say that grog emanates from an earlier period than Old Grogram.
instructions:
1. Shake all ingredients with ice.
2. into ice-filled glass.

name: Guillotine
description: The Guillotine is a mezcal cocktail recipe that combines the spirit with Cynar and dry vermouth.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled and diluted.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Gunshop Fizz
description: The Gunshop Fizz dates to 2009 in New Orleans. It caught everyone’s attention, and no wonder. The improbable Gunshop Fizz uses a full two ounces of Peychaud’s bitters, which is usually used only in dashes. It’s enough to make the same drink’s use of Sanbitter, a bright-red bitter Italian soda, seem almost dull. The rest of the drink includes lemon juice, simple syrup, strawberries, cucumbers and several twists of orange and grapefruit. It was a through-the-looking glass take on the Pimm’s Cup.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the Sanbitter in a mixing glass. Muddle and set aside for two minutes.
2. Add ice to mixing glass and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
4. Top with Sanbitter.

name: Halekulani
description: A cross between a classic bourbon sour and a tiki drink
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish
garnish: pineapple wedge, citrus wheel, or pineapple fronds, for garnish

name: Hanky Panky
description: The Hanky-Panky was created at a London hotel bar in the early 20th century for Sir Charles Hawtrey, a Victorian and Edwardian actor who mentored Noël Coward.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.

name: Happy Bastard
description: A lighter take on the Suffering Bastard cocktail recipe that calls on cucumber tonic water in place of ginger beer.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients, except tonic, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
3. Top with tonic.

name: Hard Sell
description: The Hard Sell cocktail recipe combines gin, St-Germain elderflower liqueur, Malört (Chicago's famous shot) and lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express a grapefruit peel over the surface of the drink and discard.

name: Harvard
description: A brandy twist on a Manhattan that stands out with seltzer
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, vermouth, and bitters over ice and stir until chilled
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
3. Top with soda water and garnish

name: Harvey Wallbanger
description: The Harvey Wallbanger was created in 1969 as a marketing campaign to drive sales of Galliano. A cartoon character was commissioned for the campaign, with the tagline: "Harvey Wallbanger is the name. And I can be made!". The Harvey Wallbanger character was a surfer, appearing in various ads during the campaign, and was mentioned in print as early as 1969, continuing into the 1970s.
instructions:
1. Stir the vodka and orange juice with ice in the glass
2. Float the Galliano on top
3. Garnish and serve

name: Haymaker
description: This rich combo of rye whiskey, espresso, and cream drinks like a boozy iced latte.
instructions: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker, fill with ice, and shake well. Double strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish with a large dollop of fresh whipped cream, a sprinkle of Maldon salt, and instant espresso powder.
garnish: Whipped cream, sea salt, instant coffee powder

lines.note: freshly brewed, or sub a coffee concentrate

name: Heart of Stone
description: This Boulevardier variation was the result of a last-minute menu change, quickly coming together 30 minutes before service began.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to mixing glass with ice and stir.
2. Strain over a large ice cube in a glass.
3. Garnish.

name: Hemingway Daiquiri
description: A bittersweet twist on the rum classic, with a storied past
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker over cracked ice
2. Shake until the sides are frosty
3. Strain into a coupe and garnish with a lime wedge

name: Hemingway Special
description: Ernest Hemingway, who stayed in Cuba, tried the Floridita's signature drink, the Floridita Daiquiri, and said "That's good but I prefer it without sugar and double rum," which became a cocktail now known as the Hemingway Daiquiri or the Papa Doble. This recipe was later modified further, adding grapefruit juice to the mix, at which point the drink was dubbed the "Hemingway Special".
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a shaker with ice. Shake well and strain into a large cocktail glass.

name: Highland Diver
description: If you thought Scotch whisky would be out of place at a luau, think again. The whisky’s smoky backbone plays well with the sweetness and acidity of pineapple and lemon, while the coconut and honey add body and richness to this take on the tropical classic Pearl Diver.
instructions: 1. Shake all of the ingredients with ice, strain into a mug filled with crushed ice, then garnish.
garnish: Fresh pineapple wedge and grated nutmeg

name: Home on the Range
description:
It’s back to basics with another delicious simple recipe!

I have really fallen in love with built-in-glass drinks. These are just constructed and mixed in a standard rocks glass or whatever you’re drinking from, and requires no additional equipment to stir, shake, or strain.

Not only is it ultra simple with fewer things to wash, the extra potency to start sets the mood and anchors your palate for the rest of the drink as you slowly sip. I personally looove the super spirit-forward libations, and this intensity actually helps keep me from drinking it too quickly (often a problem for me for cocktails!). Something about the more rustic nature of it compared to a carefully chilled stirred&strained cocktail just really hits the spot for me.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into a rocks glass
2. Stir to combine
3. Add a large ice cube and give it all a stir to chill
4. Finish with both a lemon and orange twist, making sure the peel oil is expressed into the surface

name: Honeyed Coffee Gin & Tonic
description: In the Honeyed Coffee Gin & Tonic, flavor fireworks happen when cold-brew coffee and the classic gin and tonic collide.
instructions:
1. Fill a glass with ice. Stir to chill the glass, then strain out the melted water.
2. Combine the coffee, honey syrup and gin in the glass.
3. Stir to chill, then top with tonic water
4. Add more ice as needed and twist a lemon peel over the top of the drink and use as a garnish.

name: Honeymoon
description: A bright and balanced sour built on apple brandy
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

name: Hoodwinked
description: This pineapple mezcal cocktail is a vacation libation. In it, Aperol plays up the bitter notes of the pineapple juice.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake and double strain into a glass over ice.
3. Garnish.
garnish: Harissa spice–coated pineapple slice, 2 pineapple fronds

name: Horse’s Neck
description: Dating back to the 1890s, it was a non-alcoholic mixture of ginger ale, ice and lemon peel. By the 1910s, brandy, or bourbon would be added for a "Horse's Neck with a Kick" or a "Stiff Horse's Neck". The non-alcoholic version was still served in upstate New York in the late 1950s and early 60s, but eventually it was phased out.
instructions:
1. Pour Cognac and ginger ale directly into a highball glass with ice cubes.
2. Stir gently.
3. If preferred, add dashes of Angostura Bitter.
garnish: Garnish with a rind of one lemon spiral.

name: Hot Buttered Rum
description: A number of flavored batters kick up this Hot Buttered Rum cocktail recipe.
instructions:
1. To a tempered mug, add 2 tablespoons of batter.
2. Top with hot water and stir in the spirit to incorporate.
3. Garnish with a cinnamon stick.

name: Hot Oaxacan Penicillin
description: Combining ginger, honey, and scotch, the Penicillin cocktail is a natural favorite for winter sipping. But looking to make an even more warming version of the modern classic, this one switches out the scotch with tequila and mezcal and turns up the heat for this Hot Oaxacan Penicillin.
instructions: 1. Add the tequila, mezcal, ginger syrup, and honey syrup to a tempered mug and top with hot water. Garnish.

name: Hot Toddy
description: This version of the hot toddy recipe is a template prime for riffing with a base of any dark spirit, hot water, citrus, honey and spices.
instructions:
1. Add spirit and honey or maple syrup to a mug.
2. Top with hot water and stir gently to dissolve honey or maple syrup.
3. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick.

name: House of Gucci Mane
description: This take on the French Martini elevates the cocktail's sweet notes, but rounds them out with an amaro base, sherry, and lime juice.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish.

name: How Bout Them Salty Apples
description: This is the perfect Fall drink- bitter, sweet, complex, and incorporates apples and Bonal.
instructions:
1. Stir ingredients with ice for 30 seconds
2. Serve over large rock

name: Hugo Spritz
description: The Hugo was conceived in 2005 in Naturns, as an alternative to Spritz Veneziano, and quickly spread beyond the borders of South Tyrol. Initially, the recipe provided for the use of lemon balm syrup, then in practice replaced by elderflower syrup, more easily available.
instructions: Combine everything in wine glass with ice

name: Humuhumunukunukuapua'a
description: This drink is hard to say but easy to drink. If you're wondering, Hawaii's state fish is the namesake.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with crushed ice

name: Hurricane
description: A surprisingly simple and unique tiki drink that’s long been misunderstood
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake vigorously
2. Pour into a tall chilled glass full of crushed ice and garnish

name: Hurricane
description: The Hurricane was created in New Orleans back in the 1940s. It was created out of necessity, when whiskey was in short supply due to the war. Rum was in abundance, and some suppliers would only sell a case of whiskey if it was accompanied by two cases of rum. Bars then had plenty of rum on hand, which forced them to get creative to move the stock!This drink is large and boozy but you can always halve the measurements for a more responsible version.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients to your cocktail shaker
2. Whip shake with pebble ice to chill and dilute
3. Pour over pebble ice into a hurricane glass
4. Top with more pebble ice
garnish: Garnish with a lemon wheel, or pineapple & maraschino

name: Illegal
instructions: Pour all ingredients into the shaker. Shake vigorously with ice.  Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, or “on the rocks” in a traditional clay or terracotta mug.

name: I’m on Fire
description: This take on the spicy Margarita cocktail recipe calls on mezcal in place of tequila and Cholula to up the heat.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with ancho chili powder and a pineapple leaf.

name: Income Tax
description: An old-timey double dose of vermouth
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker and shake for about ten seconds
2. Strain into a cocktail glass and garnish
garnish:
dashes angostura bitters

orange wedge for garnish

name: Industry Sour
description: The Industry Sour was created in St. Louis in 2011 for another industry person and the thought going into it was simply “what would happen if I put all my favorite things into one drink” usually this thought leads nowhere good but on this occasion it created a legendary drink.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into a shaking tin.
2. Add ice.
3. Shake for 8-10 seconds.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Enjoy!

name: Insanely Good Gin & Tonic
description: A Gin & Tonic cocktail recipe adds a measure of Suze, the herbal liqueur, for added bitterness in the effervescent classic.
instructions:
1. Add gin, Suze, lime cordial and bitters to a chilled Collins glass.
2. Top with ice and tonic.
3. Garnish with a lime wheel

name: Irish Coffee
description: Caffeinated alcoholic drink consisting of Irish whiskey, hot coffee, and sugar, stirred, and topped with cream (sometimes cream liqueur) The coffee is drunk through the cream.
instructions:
1. Warm black coffee is poured into a pre-heated Irish coffee glass.
2. Whiskey and at least one teaspoon of sugar is added and stirred until dissolved.
3. Fresh thick chilled cream is carefully poured over the back of a spoon held just above the surface of the coffee.
4. The layer of cream will float on the coffee without mixing.
5. Plain sugar can be replaced with sugar syrup

name: Irish Coffee
description: First introduced to the United States by way of San Francisco, the Irish Coffee was invented at Foynes Airport in 1943. At the time, Foynes acted as a major intercontinental hub to the U.K. and, one evening, when a flight bound for Newfoundland was forced to turn back due to poor weather, airport staff led the returning passengers to the airport’s cafe. The chef greeted the travelers with glasses of warm coffee laced with Irish Whiskey, which he appropriately christened the “Irish Coffee.” Eventually, Foynes Flying Boat Station was closed and the Shannon Airport took its place, where the national cocktail still greets weary travelers today. The drink finally made its way to the U.S. in 1952.
instructions:
1. Prepare an Irish Coffee glass (or a wine glass or mug) by filling it with hot water.
2. Discard hot water, and drop in sugar cubes (or sugar).
3. Add hot coffee and stir to dissolve sugar.
4. Add Irish whiskey and stir again.
5. Gently ladle a collar of lightly whipped cream to float on top of the drink.

name: Irish Maid
description: The Irish Maid is a Whiskey Sour variation featuring Irish whiskey, lemon juice and fresh cucumber. It makes the case for whiskey as a summer drink.
instructions:
1. Muddle the cucumber slices in a shaker.
2. Add the Irish whiskey, St-Germain, lemon juice and simple syrup into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice.

name: Italicus Spritz
description: A luscious cocktail that's begging for poolside.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except soda to a glass filled with ice
2. Stir to combine and top with soda

name: Jack Rose
description: This simple sweet-tart classic delivers full on apple flavor
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice and shake
2. Strain into a coupe, serve up

name: Jägerita
description: I know it’s a frat boy drink, but unless you’ve had it coming out of your nose at 4 in the morning and can’t physically drink the stuff, there’s no way you can look me in the eye and tell me that you don’t like Jägermeister because you’re a liar and I won’t believe you. Shoot it, sip it, I’ll take it any way I can get it.
instructions: Shake ingredients over cracked ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Jägermeister Negroni
description: In this nontraditional take on the classic Negroni cocktail recipe, Jägermeister stands in for Campari.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

name: Jamaican Milk Punch
description: For sweet, creamy decadence, blend up a batch of Jamaican Milk Punch with this easy adaptation.
instructions: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a sealable container, mix well, then chill for at least 6 hours. Before serving, mix briefly in a blender without ice until light and fluffy. Serve over ice cubes and garnish with freshly grated nutmeg.

name: Japanese cocktail
description: The Japanese cocktail is notorious for a handful of things: it's a very old cocktail, published in 1862; it was the first mixed drink to be named something other than “Whiskey Cocktail”, “Brandy Cocktail”, or some other similarly obvious epithet; and finally, it was the first cocktail to feature more than a dash of a fancy sweetener, orgeat.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir
2. Strain into a coupe, serve up

name: Jasmine
description: This cocktail recipe was named after Matt Jasmin. It features gin, Campari, Cointreau and lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the lemon twist in a cocktail shaker three-quarters filled with ice.
2. Shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with the lemon twist.

name: Jimmy Dean
description: This brunch cocktail plays off the classic southern flavors of sweet tea and mint, and adds orange juice, bourbon and honey liqueur to the mix.
instructions: Fill a shaker with ice. Bruise 3 mint leaves between your fingers, then add them to the shaker. Add bourbon, Bärenjäger and orange juice. Shake and strain into a chilled, ice-filled Collins glass. Top with brewed tea, then garnish.

name: John Collins
description: A John Collins is a cocktail which was attested in 1869, but may be older. It is believed to have originated with a headwaiter of that name in Mayfair, London, around 1790–1817.
instructions:
Pour all ingredients directly into a highball filled with ice. Stir gently.

NOTE:

Use ‘Old Tom’ Gin for Tom Collins.
garnish: Garnish with a lemon slice and maraschino cherry.

name: Juliet & Romeo
description: A gin cocktail recipe that would appeal to gin haters. A mix of gin, lime juice, cucumber, sugar, mint, salt and rose water.
instructions:
1. Combine cucumber and salt in a mixing tin and muddle.
2. Add all remaining ingredients and shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with mint leaf, 1 dash of rosewater on the mint leaf and 3 dashes of Angostura bitters.
garnish: mint leaf, 1 dash of rosewater, 3 dashes of Angostura bitters.

name: Jungle Bird
description: A tiki cocktail lush with pineapple and lime - plus a hint of Campari's bitterness. The Jungle Bird took off first in 1978 in Kuala Lumpur, but it wasn't until it was resurrected in 2002 that it got back on the radar. This recipe perfectly employs our Pineapple Gum Syrup!
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add a few pieces of ice and whip shake for 5 seconds
3. Strain into a glass filled with crushed ice

name: Jungle Cruise
description: This tropical highball with pineapple, gin, Campari, and bubbly is the delicious result of when the French 75 meets the Jungle Bird.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients, except the sparkling wine, to a shaker.
2. Break up 2 ice cubes with a rolling pin or muddler until they are in small pieces.
3. Add ice to the shaker, close, and whip shake until you can no longer hear the clacking ice inside the shaker.
4. Open the shaker and pour in the sparkling wine.
5. Then pour directly into the glass.
6. Garnish.

name: Jungle Spritz
description: A refreshing apertivo inspired by the classic tiki drink, the Jungle Bird.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except soda to a glass filled with ice
2. Stir to combine and top with soda

name: Ken Burns Effect
description: This cocktail recipe is a riff on the Manhattan that swaps vermouth for Dry Sack sherry, a blend of Oloroso and PX and maraschino liqueur.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir.
2. Strain and pour into a coupe glass.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

name: Kentucky Flyer
description: The Kentucky Flyer is a variation on the classic Aviation cocktail that subs rye whiskey for gin.
instructions:
1. Add the rye whiskey, maraschino liqueur and lemon juice to a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass or coupe.
garnish: Garnish with 2 brandied cherries and a mint sprig speared on a pick.

name: Keoke Coffee
description: An updated take on the Keoke Coffee cocktail recipe, which adds brandy to the mix and gets served in an Irish Coffee glass.
instructions:
1. In a preheated Irish Coffee glass, add crème de cacao, brandy and brown sugar syrup.
2. Top up with hot coffee, leaving room for cream.
3. Finish with a generous float of whipped cream.

name: Keystone Highball
description: Like any thoughtful pairing, this dinner cocktail recipe can be adjusted to suit the meal at hand.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball or Collins glass two-thirds full with ice.
2. Stir to chill the glass, then drain off any water.
3. Pour the tea, St-Germain and whiskey into the glass and stir gently to combine.
4. Pour soda water down the side of the glass so as to retain carbonation.
5. Add ice and top with a final splash of soda water.
6. Express the lemon peel, then discard.
7. Garnish with fresh bay leaf.
garnish: lemon peel, fresh bay leaf (or another fresh herb to complement the meal)

name: Kingston Club
description: Drambuie gets top billing in this tropical recipe, alongside pineapple, lime, Fernet Branca, Angostura and soda.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients, except the soda water, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Garnish with orange twist.

name: Kingstone Negroni
description: First created in 2009 in New York, the Kingston Negroni was an immediate hit. Smith & Cross overproof Jamaican rum swaps in for gin in a classic Negroni spec; it is no shrinking violet, so it stands up to the bombastic chocolate and bitter orange notes in the vermouth while drying out the Campari’s richness and tempering its bitterness.
instructions: Combine all ingredients and stir with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube and garnish with a long, trimmed orange peel.

name: KIR
description: In France it is usually drunk as an apéritif before a meal or snack. It was originally made with Bourgogne Aligoté, a white wine of Burgundy, but today various white wines are used throughout France, according to the region and the barkeeper. Many prefer a white Chardonnay-based Burgundy, such as Chablis.
instructions:
Pour Crème de cassis into glass, top up with white wine.

Note:

KIR ROYAL – Use Champagne instead of white wine

name: Kiwi Swizzle
description: Kiwi is underrated and underused! Tiki is the obvious first cocktail style to work kiwi in to, plus tiki and kiwi are surprisingly similar words... Fun! Chartreuse's herbal explosion is tempered by the unrefined cane character of our Demerara Gum Syrup. This is a stellar and novel tropical cocktail.
instructions:
Muddle kiwi and syrup in the bottom of highball glass
Add remaining ingredients and crushed ice until glass is about two-thirds full
Stir 20 seconds and top with more crushed ice and garnish

name: Kiwito
description: This extra-fruity riff on the classic Mojito recipe swaps out the traditional white rum for a split base of Brazilian cachaça and rhum agricole.
instructions: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker and gently muddle the kiwi. Add ice and shake vigorously for 10 seconds. Fine strain into a glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish.

name: Koffie Van Brunt
description: This hot, rum-based cocktail recipe reads like an unorthodox twist on an Irish Coffee. The drink is topped with a cream float.
instructions:
1. Fill a 12-ounce heat-proof mug halfway with boiling water.
2. Drop a small mixing tin directly into the water to create a double boiler effect.
3. Add the rum, Cherry Heering and simple syrup into the tin and let sit while preparing a shot of espresso.
4. Once the espresso is ready, pour the hot water out of the mug and pour the contents of the tin directly into the mug.
5. Add five ounces of hot water and top with the espresso shot.
6. Shake two ounces of cream in a cocktail shaker until thick but pourable and carefully pour on top of the drink.
7. Garnish with grated orange zest and cinnamon.

name: La Concha
description: A classic Piña Colada flavor profile, modeled after fino sherries. Swapping in coconut water for coconut cream and adding in Lustau fino sherry makes it light, dry, and completely crushable on a patio.
instructions:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in shaker with ice, then shake to chill.
2. Strain over crushed ice in a Collins glass.

name: La Dominicana
description: A rich, complex, rum soaked upgrade on the White Russian
instructions:
1. Whip together a wet cream using a whisk or stand mixer
2. Add rum and coffee liqueur to a mixing glass and stir over ice
3. Strain into a cocktail glass and float whipped cream on top

name: La Louisiane
description: The La Louisiane cocktail is an improvement on the Sazerac! Absinthe, rye whiskey and vermouth make this spirit-forward cocktail a stunner.
instructions: Add all ingredients to a cocktail mixing glass (or any other type of glass). Fill the mixing glass with 1 handful ice and stir continuously for 30 seconds until very cold.

name: La Rosita
description: This slightly bitter combination shows how complex a cocktail can be, even when made with fairly basic ingredients.
instructions:
1. Stir ingredients in a mixing tin with ice
2. Strain into a glass filled with cracked ice and garnish

name: Lantern Fly
description: The Lantern Fly is an easy rum cocktail recipe combining Jamaican pot still rum, amaro and lemon and ginger juices.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with candied ginger.

lines.note: such as Doctor Bird Jamaican rum

name: Last word
description: While the drink eventually fell out of favor, it enjoyed a renewed popularity after being rediscovered in 2004 and becoming a cult hit in the Seattle area.
instructions: Add all ingredients into a cocktail shaker. Shake with ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
garnish: Cherry at the bottom of the cocktail

name: Lavender & Espresso
description: This sophisticated and moody variation on the Espresso Martini introduces a lavender syrup and balances the additional sweetness with Averna, whose bold flavors prevent the drink from being just another sweet Martini.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake.
2. Strain into the glass over a large ice rock.
3. Garnish.

name: Layover in Paris
description: A simple spritz recipe that suggests a leisurely afternoon in the French capital.
instructions: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in an ice-filled wine glass and stir gently to combine, then garnish.

name: Left Hand
description: The Left Hand is a Manhattan/Negroni mash up (bourbon whiskey, Campari, sweet vermouth & chocolate bitters) from the early 2000s. It shares an almost identical ingredients list with the Boulevardier (bourbon whiskey, Campari & sweet vermouth), but the ratios are slightly skewed, favouring the 2:1 Manhattan specs in relation to the whiskey and vermouth. It went on to become a modern classic and was part of a series of "hand" cocktails - The Right Hand featured an aged rum, Tres Hand was made with mezcal and tequila, and the Smoking Hand contained an Islay and Highland whisky.
instructions:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the ingredients
2. Stir with ice for 15-30 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled stemmed cocktail glass

name: Lemon drop Martini
description: The drink was invented sometime in the 1970s in San Francisco, California. Some variations of the drink exist, such as blueberry and raspberry lemon drops. It is served at some bars and restaurants in the United States, and in such establishments in other areas of the world.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.
garnish: Garnish with sugar rim around the glass.

name: Leña
description: This cocktail recipe merges a spicy Margarita and a Jungle Bird into a tropical mezcal drink.
instructions:
1. Rim a rocks glass with Tajín and set aside.
2. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
4. Garnish with a pineapple half-wheel.
garnish: Tajín (to rim the glass), pineapple half-wheel

lines.note: combine equal parts agave nectar and hot water

name: Limoncello Spritz
description: Limoncello Spritz is a refreshing and easy Italian cocktail made with Limoncello liqueur and sparkling water.
instructions: 1. Build all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.

name: Lite Treason
description: This twist on the White Russian plays off coffee’s chocolatey, earthy notes with the addition of amaro and a mezcal-infused whipped cream.
instructions:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the vodka, coffee liqueur and amaro.
2. Stir with ice and strain into a rocks glass with one large ice cube, then top with the whipped cream. Garnish.

Mezcal Whipped Cream: Whip ½ cup of heavy cream with ½ oz. of mezcal until thick, then add rich simple syrup [2:1] to taste.

name: Little Italy
description:
This drink is a homage to the New York City’s Little Italy neighborhood. Garnish with brandied cherries and let a little of the cherry liquid dribble into the glass.

Not gonna lie – the Little Italy a love-it-or-hate it flavor. If you’re a fan of bitter flavors and you’re looking for an alternative to yet another Negroni, it may just be up your alley. It really is a superb after-dinner drink, where the medicinal overtones can be explained away as part of the history of the digestíf as a post-meal tummy-soother.

Make sure to have very fresh vermouth on hand for this drink; it’s bitter enough without the acrid tang of old vermouth.
instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice for about 20 seconds. Strain into a small chilled cocktail glass and garnish with a cherry or a piece of marinated artichoke heart.

name: Lone Ranger
description: The Lone Ranger is a French 75 cocktail made with tequila in place of gin or Cognac and brut rosé sparkling wine.
instructions:
1. Add the tequila, lemon juice and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until cold.
2. Add the sparkling wine to the cocktail shaker.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a Collins glass.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Long Island Ice Tea
description: The cocktail has been criticized for its large number of ingredients, making it cumbersome to prepare in busy bars. It is considered a favorite of university students in the United States and it has thus garnered negative connotations as "an act of mixological atrocity favored by college students and wastrels", in the words of one food critic.
instructions:
Add all ingredients into a highball glass filled with ice.
Stir gently.

name: Love & Murder
description: Two polarising liqueurs come together resulting in a herbaceous, bittersweet concoction. Whilst it does have a decent amount of sugar in the drink the strong flavours keep you intrigued.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Double strain into a coupe glass

name: Lucien Gaudin
description: Introducing the Lucien Gaudin. Named for an early 20th century French Olympic fencer, the Lucien Gaudin starts off in the manner of a Negroni by combining gin with Campari. With the addition of Cointreau and dry vermouth the result is a pleasantly bitter drink that is simultaneously rich and dry--a challenging flavor to create which is all the more enjoyable because of its rarity.
instructions:
1. Combine ingredients in a mixing glass and fill with ice.
2. Stir well and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
garnish: A twist of orange peel is not out of place here.

name: Lust for Life
description: This easy mezcal cocktail recipe combines the agave spirit with palo cortado sherry, orgeat, pineapple and lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with cocoa powder.

name: Mai-Tai
description: The Mai Tai has a mixed up history. Reaching its height of popularity in the 50s and 60s, it is the quintessential tiki drink. Two tiki trendsetters both claim to have invented the cocktail, though their versions are distinctly different. Over time all kinds of fruity concoctions have been whipped up under the name of Mai Tai, no doubt, in all the colors of the rainbow. Although itself slightly modified, due to availability of ingredients, the ‘Original” Mai Tai reigns supreme.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into a shaker with ice.
2. Shake and pour into a double rocks glass or a highball glass.

*The Martinique molasses rum used in the original was not an Agricole rum but a type of “rummy” from molasses.*
garnish: Garnish with pineapple spear, mint leaves, and lime peel.

name: Mamie Taylor

name: Manager's Meeting

instructions: Muddle cucumber and honey syrup in the bottom of a cocktail shaker. Add the mango puree and lime juice and shake with ice vigorously. Strain into a copper mug. Top with ginger beer and stir.

name: Manhattan
description: Popular history suggests that the drink originated at the Manhattan Club in New York City in the mid-1870s, where it was invented for a banquet hosted by Jennie Jerome (Lady Randolph Churchill, mother of Winston) in honor of presidential candidate Samuel J. Tilden. The success of the banquet made the drink fashionable, later prompting several people to request the drink by referring to the name of the club where it originated—"the Manhattan cocktail". However, Lady Randolph was in France at the time and pregnant, so the story is likely a fiction.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

As a Cuban mojito riff, it has the essential mojito ingredients like mint, rum, and club soda, but adds tropical flavor with the passionfruit syrup. name: Margarita
description: The true Margarita—a blend of fresh lime juice, tequila and orange liqueur with an optional sweetener—is a potent, well-built entry in the cocktail canon. Plenty claim credit for its invention: a restaurateur based south of Tijuana in the 1930s, a socialite in Acapulco in the 1940s. Others believe it evolved as a south-of-the-border twist on the then-popular Daisy (the Spanish word for “daisy” is “Margarita,” after all), dreamed up during Prohibition when Americans would travel abroad to drink. The Margarita was named Esquire’s cocktail of the month in December 1953, and it has hardly flagged in popularity since, rising in stature alongside tequila, which got a pop-culture boost from the Eagles (“Tequila Sunrise”), Rolling Stones (the Cocaine and Tequila Sunrise Tour of ’72), and of course, Jimmy Buffet (“Margaritaville”).

name: Michelada
description:
Beer is great. That is unassailable. But beer cocktails combine two wonderful categories into one drink, and that is a union everyone can get behind. Take the Michelada: This Mexican classic kicks up the flavor of beer with an assortment of accessories, including lime and hot sauce.

The Michelada’s origins are unclear, with multiple legends surrounding its creation. But it likely dates back to the middle of the 20th century when it became popular in Mexico to serve beer with lime and salt. The word itself is a combination of “chela,” which is slang for a light beer, “helada” (cold), and “mi”—essentially “my cold beer.”

Many Michelada recipes call for tomato juice or Clamato (a mixture of clam and tomato juices) to create a Bloody Mary-style drink made with beer instead of vodka. Others choose to skip the tomato juice entirely. In Mexico City, for example, the Michelada is commonly made without tomato juice and instead relies on citrus, spices and hot sauce.

This recipe aligns closer to the Mexico City version, forgoing tomato in favor of lime juice, hot sauce and seasonings. You can choose your favorite beer as the starting point, but you can’t go wrong with a Mexican lager like Tecate, Sol or Modelo Especial. Rim the glass with a salt-cayenne mixture, and you’ll have a hint of savory spice with each sip.
instructions:

2. Spread a layer of flaky salt or the chili-lime blend on a saucer. Wet the rim of a chilled beer mug or large glass by running a lime wedge around it. Dip the rim of the glass in the seasoning or salt, rolling it around to cover the entire circumference.
3. Fill the glass about halfway with ice, then add the lime juice, chili sauce, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir to combine all of the ingredients.
4. Slowly pour the beer into the glass. Garnish with lime wedge and serve immediately.

name: Monkey Gland
description:
Many themes surrounding innovation, industry, and culture have captured the imagination of bartenders; take for example the 20th Century or Blood and Sand. In this case, it is medicine that lent inspiration, as the monkey gland was named in honor of a procedure that gained quite a bit of attention in the 1920s. Pioneered by Dr. Serge Voronoff, the process involved transplanting a monkey's sexual gland tissue into humans, and carried the promise of “rejuvenation” in the form of youthful energy, prolonged life, and other various health claims. An increase in sexual ability was also implied, and undoubtedly a focus of interest. The practice of inserting monkey glands into millionaires' bodies fascinated the public, and references to the technique crept into popular culture—from film, to literature, to beverage culture—and resulted in this drink, which was created in Paris. The drink was a hit among bar patrons, who were often American expats. 

A simple mix of gin, orange, grenadine, and absinthe , this drink delivers a beautiful candy-orange color. However, the monkey gland has a bit of a reputation taste-wise: the ingredients don’t quite work together, and our experience with the drink was roughly the same. Anise and orange are odd bedfellows and it feels as though the absinthe never quite fits in with the other ingredients. The nose is full of orange and absinthe, followed by a fruity and herbal sip. The mixture results in a sweet tart flavor, almost candy like, with a juniper finish. It has the same overall roundness as other orange juice based drinks, such as the income tax or Blood and Sand, and the absinthe does shine in providing a sharpness that cuts through the roundness, which is a nice touch. 

The drink is often mixed one of two ways: equal parts gin and orange juice (the classic ratio) or 2:1, which has become popular over time. Our tastes tend toward the modern, although the 1:1 ratio seems to more successfully smooth out the absinthe bumps. Some recipes use Benedictine in place of absinthe, likely from a little ingenuity during periods of absinthe unavailability. This does suit some tastes better, so it is worth trying. We understand why recipes call for a specific type of gin—this funky drink can definitely hinge on the variety selected. Many recipes recommend Plymouth gin for this—a directive we didn’t follow, but that could be good advice to adhere to, although in general a dry gin is what you want here. As always, use fresh orange juice. Some recipes suggest no garnish, which is fine, but we like a nice orange wedge on the rim for presentation.

Lemon juice introduces a touch of bright and refreshing tartness later balanced by deep molasses of demerara syrup and almond nuttiness of orgeat.

All in all, Norwegian Paralysis is a quite unique tiki cocktail with rather complex flavour profile. Delicious to the very last drop.

name: Old Fashioned
description:
Developed during the 19th century and given its name in the 1880s, it is an IBA Official Cocktail.

Old-Fashioned is as traditional as they come. A simple mix of spirits, sugar, bitters and water, it appears in 1806 as the first printed recipe for a cocktail (“cock tail”). Other alcohols were permitted, but the whiskey or rye version of this combination, over ice, is what we now know as the Old Fashioned, thought to be named later that century after more elaborate new-fangled cocktails entered the canon. During Prohibition, the recipe veered into odd territory, adding fruit and cherries to distract from the available crude spirits. After repeal, it was the imposter version that stuck until the recent cocktail revival brought the original recipe back from the brink of extinction.

Other variants of the cocktail include those created with fruits like pineapple or plants such as coca leaves.

name: Ramos Fizz
description: Created in New Orleans around 1888 or so, this cocktail was originally known as the New Orleans Fizz. The drink was meant to be shaken for anywhere from two to twelve full minutes—depending on whom you ask—to achieve a fluffy, meringue-like texture. Bars of the day achieved this yeoman’s task by creating bartender relays, where lines of “shaker men” would pull off the athletic endeavor. By 1915’s Mardi Gras season, the drink was so popular that one bar needed thirty shaker men. This stunningly gorgeous cocktail remains no easy task for modern drink makers, so today’s bartenders have begun utilizing paint shaker–like devices and whipped cream canisters as a sort of cheat. But if you have two strong arms, you can shake up a fine drink.
