4. Express orange oil atop the drink before serving.
5. Garnish.

name: Red Hook
description: This contemporary Manhattan riff is a balanced people-pleaser
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up

name: Red Morning Light
description: Smoky scotch and bittersweet Campari combine for the perfect cold-weather sipper from Vegas.
instructions:
1. Stir all of the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice until chilled.
2. Strain into a glass holding a large ice cube.
3. Use an atomizer to spray the drink with a smoky scotch, then garnish. (Alternately, drip several drops of scotch atop the drink, then garnish.)

name: Remember the Alimony
description: A split base of fino sherry and Cynar are finished with a measure of gin for a thoroughly modern sherry cocktail recipe.
instructions:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the orange twist in a rocks glass filled with one large piece of ice.
2. Stir until chilled, about 30 seconds.
3. Express an orange twist over the drink and drop into the glass.

name: Remember the Maine
description: This rye-based cocktail recipe has an ingredient list that’s part Sazerac, part Manhattan and has a grandiose backstory to boot.
instructions:
1. In a chilled coupe or cocktail glass, add a dash of absinthe. Roll around to coat and discard excess.
2. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
3. Add ice and stir well.
4. Strain into prepared coupe or cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: Reno
description: The story which inspired this cocktail took place during WWII on 21st April 1945, when the allied forces planned to retake Bologna. Polish, English, American and French troops helped Italian partisans to capture the city in a very unusual battlefield, a river called Reno. I used ingredients that remind me of the forces involved in the battle. Amaro Montenegro symbolises the city. Cocchi Americano to celebrate the partisan's movement born in Asti. Italicus represents braveness. And finally, Suze, this sophisticated liqueur de gentian, used to remember the aid received by the allies. Without this strong bitter touch, my cocktail wouldn't be the same, and the battle wouldn't have been won!
instructions:
1. Throw all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into over a large cube ice.
3. Garnish.

name: Revolver
description: A San Francisco original, and an exceptional coffee-laced riff on the Manhattan
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir around 15 seconds
2. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish

name: Rib Tickler
description: This drink was born out of the idea to create a more sippable, bubbly White Negroni (which is Suze, gin, and Lillet Blanc or blanc vermouth).
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all ingredients
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a wine glass
4. Top with soda water

name: Ric Pear Blanc
description: This drink accents blanc vermouth’s floral, fruity characteristics with the flavors of pear and ginger.
instructions:
1. Shake all of the ingredients without ice until foamy, then add ice to the shaker and shake again until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled glass, and garnish.

name: Risorgimento d’Italia
description: A more spiritous twist on the Garibaldi cocktail recipe, this drink sees additions of gin and absinthe to the orange juice and Campari.
instructions:
1. Combine the first four ingredients in a Collins glass, then stir and add spear ice (or cubes).
2. Using an atomizer, spritz the absinthe over the top of the drink.
3. Garnish with an orange slice sprinkled with salt.

name: Ritz Cocktail
description: The Ritz Cocktail, created in 1985, bears the DNA of traditional classics, and it helped usher in a new wave of talented bartenders.
instructions: 1. Combine the first 4 ingredients in a shaker and fill with ice. Shake well to chill, then strain into a chilled glass. Top with Champagne and garnish.

name: Rob Roy No. 3
description: This overhaul of a classic scotch whisky cocktail recipe is inspired by the structure of a "perfect" cocktail.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.

name: Rocinante
description: Named after Don Quixote's horse, this mezcal sipper blends smoky, bitter, floral, and sweet notes that tell a story of exploration and timeless landscapes.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir and strain over a large cube in a glass.
3. Garnish.

name: Rocket Power
instructions: Add arugula into your shaking tin, add ice, and shake for 10 seconds. Add remaining ingredients, shake until chilled. Double strain into chilled glass over fresh ice.

name: Roman Holiday
description:
Jungle Bird is a quintessential tiki / tropical cocktail. The combination of blackstrap rum and Campari is incredibly effective, delivering that bitter-sweet satisfaction. Roman Holiday – draws inspiration from this delicious creation and reinterprets it in a rather unique and tasty way. (I have encountered a few different specs for this cocktail. I chose to test this one, simply because I happened to find it first, but there might be other, even mores delicious riffs).

Base of this cocktail is split between London dry gin and amaro Averna. Gin brings dry notes of juniper, touch of coriander, while Averna adds bold herbal flavours with hints of aniseed and chocolate. Campari, provides those bitter-sweet notes of Mediterranean oranges, without which it is hard to imagine the cocktail world. Pineapple juice brings that delicious tropical fruity sweetness with a touch of acidity, while tartness of the lime juice, balances out the cocktail. Last addition of cold brew, increases the cocktail complexity and gives it an almost Americano kind of vibe. Not too dominating, just a subtle touch lingering in the background.

All in all, Roman Holiday, is a rather unique and tasty creation. Drawing inspiration from a tiki classic, yet completely reimagining it. This certainly piqued my interest to try the other available specs for this cocktail side by side, to see which taste best.
instructions:
1. Fill a cocktail shaker with gin, Amaro, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and cold brew coffee. Add ice to the shaker.
2. Shake well until the mixture is chilled.
3. Fill a glass with crushed ice.
4. Strain the cocktail over the crushed ice.
5. Garnish with pineapple leaves and a cinnamon stick that's been charred on the edge with a lighter or blowtorch. Serve the cocktail immediately.

name: Rome With a View
description: The Rome With a View cocktail recipe falls somewhere between an afternoon appropriate Collins and an Americano.
instructions:
1. Add Campari, dry vermouth, lime juice and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange wheel.

name: Room Key
description: It’s basically a Skeleton Key with white rum instead of whiskey.
instructions: Shake on ice and pour into a Collins glass over ice. Top with Mineral Water and then add all the angostura dashes to the top. Serve with a straw.

name: Royal Hawaiian
description: A tropical gin cocktail recipe, the Royal Hawaiian is reimagined here, with the pineapple drink served on crushed ice.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker.
2. Add a handful of pebble ice and whip-shake.
3. Pour into a chilled double rocks glass, and top with more pebble ice.
4. Garnish with a mint bouquet and serve with a straw.

name: Rubino Tequila Spritz
description: The ruby-hued Rubino Spritz complements earthy tequila with the floral and citrus notes of Italian bergamot liqueur Italicus, all amplified by the juicy sweetness of blood orange soda.
instructions: 1. Combine the first 3 ingredients in a shaker with ice. Shake and strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice. Top with blood orange soda and Prosecco, then garnish.

name: Rum and Ramazzotti
description: This cocktail is an interesting take on the classic Jungle Bird, drawing inspiration from this well-known tiki drink with a couple of key substitutions. It uses a dark rum base with pronounced molasses, caramel, coffee, chocolate, and oak notes, paired with Amaro Ramazzotti which replaces Campari. The amaro adds bitter-sweet flavors of liquorice, cola, oranges, and cinnamon. Generous pineapple juice maintains the tropical theme with sweet and tart fruitiness, while fresh lime juice provides a sharp, tart kick. The result is a slightly deeper, bolder, but nonetheless flavourful and intriguing variation.
instructions:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over fresh pebble ice.
4. Garnish with a few lime wheels, skewered cherry and pineapple spears.

name: Rum Old Fashioned
description: The oldest recipe for this cocktail appeared in cocktail guides around 1860 and called for it to be made with gin. A couple of decades later it was made with bourbon, apparently in Louisville, Kentucky. You'll love how delicious the Old Fashioned tastes when made with Reserva Exclusiva. It almost seems like the foundation of the Old Fashioned was laid out with this rum in mind. An incredible mix of rich, bitter and citrusy makes our version of rum a choice for all fans of the old fashion.
instructions: Add all ingredients to a stirring glass, fill with ice, stir and strain.

name: Russian Spring Punch
description: The Russian Spring Punch was created in London, England in the 1980s, for friends wishing to hold a cocktail party while minimizing the amount of money they had to spend on alcohol. Participants were provided with the vodka, cassis, sugar syrup and lemon juice, and were asked to bring their own sparkling wine. It is named for the russian vodka, and the Tom Collins, which is a spring drink.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker except the sparkling wine, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled tall tumbler glass filled with ice, and top up with sparkling wine.
garnish: Garnish with blackberries and optionally a lemon slice as well.

name: Rusty Nail
description:
A Rusty Nail can be served in an old-fashioned glass on the rocks, or "up" in a stemmed glass. It is most commonly served over ice. A Rusty Nail served without ice is sometimes called a Straight Up Nail.

  - **The Rusty Bob**, which substitutes Bourbon whiskey for blended Scotch whisky
  - **The Rusty Ale**, in which a shot of Drambuie is added to any beer, served without ice.
  - **The Smoky Nail**, which uses Islay whisky (very smoky in flavor) in place of blended Scotch whisky.
  - **The Clavo Ahumado** (Spanish for "smoky nail"), using mezcal instead of blended Scotch whisky.
  - **The Railroad Spike**, often served at brunch and made with approximately four parts Cold brewed coffee to one part Drambuie in a tall glass over ice.
  - **The Donald Sutherland**, which substitutes Canadian rye whisky for blended Scotch whisky.
instructions: Pour all ingredients directly into an old fashioned glass filled with ice. Stir gently.

name: Rusty Ringo
description: A modern interpretation of the Rusty Nail cocktail recipe made with calvados, Scotch and Drambuie liqueur.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir for 60 rotations.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with gold leaf.

name: Sage Gibson
description: This take on the Gibson cocktail infuses vodka with sage, an ode to the enduring harvest of the colder months.
instructions:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir to chill. Add the onion and sage to a chilled glass. Pour the cocktail into the glass.
Sage-Infused VodkaAllow fresh sage (roughly 1 leafy sprig per 8 oz) to steep and infuse vodka for 3 days.
garnish: Pickled onion and fresh sage leaf

name: Saisonnière
description: The winter version of a seasonally changing staple cocktail recipe—hence, the name Saisonnière—is an herbal riff on the basic sour.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a sage leaf and a lemon twist.
garnish: sage leaf and a lemon twist

name: Sakura Martini
description: This Martini cocktail recipe combines salted cherry blossom with maraschino and the dry, vinous quality of sake.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a glass and garnish with a salted cherry blossom.

name: Salmoncito
description: This bittersweet, citrusy highball made with gin, Campari, grapefruit and tonic is a Mexico City-born modern classic.
instructions:
1. Combine the first three ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a supremed grapefruit wedge and a grapefruit twist; express oil from the grapefruit peel and then discard it.
garnish: A supremed grapefruit wedge and a discarded grapefruit twist

name: Sang Amer
description: For something light to whet the appetite, mix together this tequila aperitif cocktail.
instructions: 1. Reverse dry shake (shake hard with ice first and then remove the ice and shake hard again) to achieve a frothy layer. Pour into an ice-filled glass. Garnish.

name: Sangria
description:
A punch, sangria traditionally consists of red wine and chopped fruit, often with other ingredients or spirits.

Sangria is very popular among foreign tourists in Spain even if locals do not consume the beverage that much. It is commonly served in bars, restaurants, and chiringuitos and at festivities throughout Portugal and Spain.
instructions:
1. Chop the orange (leaving the peel on) and apple into bite-sized chunks, then add them to the bottom of a pitcher. Sprinkle them with sugar and stir. Let them stand for 20 minutes at room temperature.
2. After 20 minutes, pour in the red wine, brandy, orange liqueur, and lemon rounds. Stir and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours. (Don’t go beyond 4 hours or the fruit texture starts to degrade.)
3. Pour the sangria into ice filled glasses and top with a splash of sparkling water (if desired). Add fruit to each glass, preferably on long skewers for easy snacking.
garnish: Drop fruit chunks into a glass

name: Saturn
description: Winner of 1967's International Bartender's Association World Cocktail Championship - The Saturn is ready for its comeback!
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice

name: Sauvignon Blanc Punch
description: This vibrant white wine meets its perfect match, Aperol, in this epic punch recipe.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except the club soda into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with fresh ice.
3. Top with the club soda and stir briefly and gently to combine.

name: Savoy Special #1
description: For those who find martinis overly dry, this variation incorporates a hint of grenadine to craft a smoother and well-balanced flavor profile.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a chilled martini glass

name: Sawyer
description: The Sawyer is an icy, bitters-soaked twist on a gimlet doctored with nearly thirty dashes of bitters.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass.

lines.note: equal parts Fee Brothers West Indian Orange Bitters and Regans' Orange Bitters No. 6

name: Sazerac
description:
The Sazerac is a local variation of a cognac or whiskey cocktail originally from New Orleans, named for the Sazerac de Forge et Fils brand of cognac brandy that served as its original main ingredient.
The drink is most traditionally a combination of cognac or rye whiskey, absinthe, Peychaud's Bitters, and sugar, although bourbon whiskey is sometimes substituted for the rye and Herbsaint is sometimes substituted for the absinthe.
Some claim it is the oldest known American cocktail, with origins in antebellum New Orleans, although some dispute this, and American instances of published usage of the word cocktail to describe a mixture of spirits, bitters, and sugar can be traced to the dawn of the 19th century.
instructions:
1. Rinse a chilled old-fashioned glass with the absinthe.
2. Add crushed ice and set it aside.
3. Stir the remaining ingredients over ice in a mixing glass.
4. Discard the ice and any excess absinthe from the prepared glass.
5. Strain the mixed drink into the glass.

lines.note: Can also split base with cognac 45-15

name: Scofflaw
description: The creatively named Scofflaw combines whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice and grenadine. It was invented in Paris during U.S. Prohibition.
instructions:
1. Add the whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice, grenadine and orange bitters into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Scorched Earth
description: A wild and daring twist on the Negroni
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir
2. Strain into a lowball or whiskey glass over ice
3. Flame orange peel (optionally) and garnish

name: Scorpion Bowl
description: The Scorpion, like many tiki cocktails, has gone through countless iterations, from a gin and wine-laced libation to this contemporary version of a 1946 recipe. It’s difficult to know where the original recipe ends and the contemporary begins, especially when so much rum is involved. But it is thought that the Scorpion was modeled on a Hawaiian punch, which mostly likely contained okolehao, an indigenous spirit distilled from the Polynesian ti plant. Orgeat is a constant ingredient in most interpretations and is key to the balance of dark rum and fruit.
instructions:
1. Put everything in a blender.
2. Blend for up to 10 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a Tiki bowl.

name: Scorpion Reef
description: The Scorpion Reef draws inspiration from a smoked pineapple flan. After swizzling, you’ve got a tropical potion with just enough overproof heat to keep you on your toes with the sensation of caramelized pineapple fresh off the grill.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except the Angostura bitters
2. Half fill with crushed / pebble ice
3. Swizzle until glass is frosted
4. Finish with Angostura bitters and five spice

name: Scotch and Coconut
description: A split base of rum and Scotch might sound like the perfect match for cold-weather sipping, but when curaçao and coconut water enter the equation, the combo takes a turn for the tropical.
instructions:
1. A day ahead of making the cocktail, freeze the coconut water in a large ice cube mold.
2. When ready to make the drink, combine the ingredients in a shaker with ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over the frozen coconut water ice.

name: Scotch Orgeat Sour
description: This interpretation of the sour calls for Scotch as the choice of spirit and orgeat as the sweetener, bringing it closer to the tiki realm.
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker, add all ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Strain over fresh ice into an old fashioned glass
garnish: Garnish with a lemon wheel and an orchid

name: Scotch Sling
description: The Improved Scotch Sling is a sour cocktail recipe that gets stirred, rather than shaken. Here, whisky meets honey, lemon and maraschino.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with a lemon peel.

name: Screwdriver
description: A screwdriver is a simple and popular alcoholic highball drink made with orange juice and vodka. In the UK, it is referred to as a "vodka and orange". While the basic drink is simply the two ingredients, there are many variations. Many of the variations have different names in different parts of the world.
instructions:
1. Add ice to tumbler glass first.
2. Add vodka and orange juice next
garnish: Garnish with slice of orange or homemade orange twists

name: Sea Breeze
description: The cocktail is usually consumed during summer months. The drink may be shaken in order to create a foamy surface.
instructions: Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
garnish: Garnish with orange zest and cherry

name: Sea Legs
description: The Sea Legs cocktail encapsulates a nautical feel without the kitsch. Big smoke flavor from the scotch and mezcal is lightened up with fresh lime and almond orgeat... and don't skip the celery bitters on this one.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a Hybrid Cocktail Shaker.
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Garnish with a salted rim and lime wheel.

name: Second Serve
description: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs. Italy matchup.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.

name: Second Serve
description: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs. Italy matchup.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.

name: See You on Wednesday
description: This zero-proof Spicy Margarita variation combines celery juice, lime juice, jalapeno, cilantro, agave nectar, and salt.
instructions:
1. At the bottom of a shaker, muddle the jalapeño, cilantro, and agave nectar.
2. Add the celery juice, lime juice, and salt solution. Add ice and shake until well chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a Tajín-rimmed double rocks glass over large-format ice.

name: Seelbach
description: The Seelbach Cocktail may not be a julep, but it doesn't have to be: it's respectable, powerful, and delicious right down to the bottom of the glass.
instructions:
1. Add the bourbon, Cointreau, Angostura bitters and Peychaud’s bitters into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled flute.
3. Top with cold Champagne or other sparkling wine.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

name: Sentimental Gentleman
description: The Sentimental Gentleman offers up a peaty smoke aroma from the Scotch that later gains walnut notes as it warms up. The malt from the Scotch fills the sip, and the swallow is an interplay of the herbal Benedictine and the walnut. Rather poetically, the Sentimental Gentleman gets a bit more bitter and sharp over time as it acclimates to room temperature.
instructions:
1. Stir all ingredients.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.

name: Seven Seas Swizzle
description: This recipe plays with green tea syrup and lime, for a riff on the Queen Park Swizzle with traditional punch ingredients.
instructions:
1. Build all the ingredients in the appropriate glass and add half the amount of necessary ice. 
2. Swizzle until the glass is cool.
3. Top with ice and garnish.
garnish: Mint bouquet and dusting of nutmeg

name: Sex on the Beach
description:
There are two general types of the cocktail:

- The IBA official cocktail is made from vodka, peach schnapps, orange juice, and cranberry juice.
- An alternative recipe is made from vodka, Chambord, Midori Melon Liqueur, pineapple juice, and cranberry juice.

The drink is built over ice in a highball glass and garnished with an orange slice. Sometimes they are mixed in smaller amounts and served as a shooter.
instructions: Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
garnish: Garnish with a half orange slice.

name: Sex Work Is Real Work
description: This cocktail recipe is a take on the frozen Pornstar Martini with additions of umami-forward umeboshi and Champagne acid.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth and serve in your glass of choice.
3. Garnish with edible flower and mint bouquet.

name: Shade Thrower
description: For a less bitter and smoother Boulevardier riff, this one swaps out the Campari with Averna and Aperol.
instructions: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass filled with a large ice cube, and garnish.

name: Shirley Temple
description: The cocktail may have been invented in West Hollywood, California, to serve then-child actress Shirley Temple.
instructions:
1. Fill a Collins glass with cubed ice.
2. Add the grenadine and lime juice.
3. Top with the ginger ale and gently stir to combine.
garnish: Garnish with two skewered Luxardo maraschino cherries.

name: Shliva Sour
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to shaker
2. Shake for 15sec
3. Strain into a glass

name: Shoot the Moon
description: A cocktail recipe for a riff on the Gin Old-Fashioned made with Fords Gin and pear brandy and designed to minimize water waste.
instructions:
1. In a double Old-Fashioned glass, combine all ingredients with ice.
2. Stir until chilled and diluted.
3. Garnish with dehydrated pear and dust with cinnamon.

name: Sidecar
description:
The exact origin of the sidecar is unclear, but it is thought to have been invented around the end of World War I in either London or Paris. The drink was directly named for the motorcycle attachment, which was very commonly used back then.

Like the daiquiri, the sidecar evolved from the original sour formula, but sidecars are often drier than sours, combining liqueurs like curaçao with citrus. Sidecars are considered more of a challenge for bartenders because the proportion of ingredients is more difficult to balance for liqueurs of variable sweetness.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Siesta
description:
This spin on the Hemingway Daiquiri was created in 2006. Tequila adds warmth to bitter Campari; it's a luxurious cocktail that's a bit like sipping candied grapefruit peel.

For those that might need two cocktails today, you can check out the Hemingway Daiquiri mentioned above, in last year's Advent of Cocktails, here: AoC 2021, Dec 12: Hemingway Daiquiri
instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled coupe

name: Sin Cyn
description: The simple Sin Cyn cocktail combines scotch with Cynar and sweet vermouth. It’s part Rob Roy, part Boulevardier and wholly delicious.
instructions:
1. Add all the ingredients into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.

name: Singapore Sling
description: This long drink was developed sometime before 1915 in Singapore. It was initially called the gin sling – a sling was originally a North American drink composed of spirit and water, sweetened and flavored.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice cubes. Shake well. Strain into Hurricane glass.
garnish: Garnish with pineapple and maraschino cherry

name: Single Village Fix
description: This three-ingredient mezcal cocktail has become a modern classic.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice
2. Shake and strain into a chilled coupe.

name: Skeleton Key
description: The Skeleton Key cocktail is the ideal blend of bourbon, elderflower, and ginger beer! This fun drink is easy to mix up right in the glass.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice (or clear ice). Pour in the bourbon, St Germain, and lemon juice. Top with the ginger beer.
2. Shake in 6 to 8 dashes Angostura bitters. Serve immediately.

name: Smoke Follows Beauty
description: This mezcal cocktail is both spicy and refreshing, thanks to serrano-infused triple sec, cucumbers, and cilantro.
instructions:
1. In a shaker, muddle the cucumber and cilantro.
2. Add the mezcal, infused triple sec, lime juice, agave syrup, and ice, and shake until well-chilled.
3. Double-strain into a Nick & Nora glass.
4. Garnish with a chilled slice of jicama seasoned with sal de gusano.

name: SmokeRoni
description: Created in Cape Town, the SmokeRoni is an Agave Negroni riff that really brings the smoke to the glass. Combining Montelobos Mezcal, Tequila, Sweet Vermouth & Campari this is a drink that captures the depth that you’ve been missing
instructions: Stir all ingredients in an ice-filled mixing glass and strain over large ice

name: Smooth Kiss
instructions:
1. Shake all ingredients except the soda water.
2. Top up with soda water

name: Snake Bit Sprout
description: In this refreshing chamomile cocktail, the flowers bring a floral depth to the mix. And did you know chamomile was once used as a southern remedy for snake bites? That's inspired the drink's name.
instructions:
1. Shake all of the ingredients except the cider with ice and strain into glass filled with 4 large ice cubes.
2. Top with crushed ice, fill with chilled cider.
3. Garnish

name: Snake Eyes
description: Inspired by the Caribbean combo of blended Scotch and coconut, this cocktail recipe swaps in smoky mezcal in lieu of whisky.
instructions:
1. Salt the rim of a large rocks glass.
2. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker, add ice, then shake until chilled.
3. Fine strain into the large rocks glass filled with ice.

name: Sno-Cone
description: The drink is a visual reference to the vibrant, fruity shaved ice and syrup Sno-Cones served on street corners in the summer. As this was for a winter menu, it has a rich and warming flavor profile. The idea was to create a deceptively seasonal drink, one that looked like summer but drank like winter.
instructions:
1. Whip shake with crushed ice and dump into the glass.
2. Top with crushed ice and garnish with a few generous dashes of Peychaud's bitters.

name: Society Street
description: As a nod to the many Manhattan variations named after New York neighborhoods, this is a Charleston-inspired take on the classic. The Society Street features a bourbon base and a hint of peach in tribute to the South with Cognac for the city's French influence.
instructions: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass, fill with ice, and stir. Strain the glass. Garnish.

name: Sour Strawberry Highball
description: Can a compelling cocktail be made with just two ingredients? This Sour Strawberry Highball, although still simple, does require some assembly. A homemade strawberry shrub brings a punch of tart sweetness, but don't stop there: you’re welcome to mingle with other spirits and other fruits in this highly modifiable highball recipe.
instructions:

Strawberry Shrub SyrupWash, trim, and quarter 1 lb. of ripe strawberries. Add to a mixing bowl with 2 cups of granulated sugar and toss to coat. Gently mash the fruit with a fork. Cover and let stand at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 1 day (but 2 is ideal), periodically shaking the container to redistribute the contents. name: Spanish Monk
description: First published in 1951, the Spanish Monk combines gin, lemon, green Chartreuse, simple syrup and an egg white.
instructions:

name: Spiced Cranberry-Orange Punch
description: For a festive spirit-free option to present at holiday parties, stir up this spiced cranberry-orange punch. Spicy ginger, warm baking spices, the herbaceousness of rosemary, and sparkling seltzer elevate this mix of cranberry and orange juices.
instructions:
1. Heat the water, sugar, ginger, rosemary sprig, cinnamon stick, and star anise in large saucepan over medium heat, stirring often, until sugar has dissolved, about 5 minutes; do not boil. Stir in cranberries and cook, stirring often, until cranberries just begin to pop open, about 3 minutes. Off heat, let cranberry mixture cool completely, about 30 minutes. Transfer to bowl or storage container, cover, and refrigerate until well chilled, at least 1 hour or up to 4 days.
2. Combine the cranberry mixture, seltzer, cranberry juice, and orange juice in large punch bowl. Add an ice ring and garnish with rosemary sprigs and orange slices. Serve in chilled punch cups.
NOTEAn ice ring does the best job of keeping the punch chilled for several hours without overdiluting. If necessary, 8 large ice cubes can be used instead.

name: St-Germain Gin & Tonic
description: This mesmerizingly azure-topped gin and tonic draws inspiration from the state of California. It calls for the Golden State's Gray Whale gin for its Californian ingredients, such as citrus and sea kelp, but a botanical forward new Western gin can also be used in its place.
instructions:

name: St. Regis Julep
description: The St. Regis Julep is a funky, awesome riff on a julep from New Orleans.

name: Step Into Liquid
description: The Step into Liquid dates to at least 2019, and it was perhaps named after the 2003 surfing documentary. While I have had other pineapple rum-Campari drinks in the Negroni ballpark, like the Pineapple Kingston Negroni, Best Fronds, and Jungle Boulevard, they all called for regular sweet vermouth instead of Punt e Mes. Once prepared, the Step into Liquid offered up orange, dark rum, pineapple, and herbal aromas to the nose. Next, grape and caramel notes on the sip gave way to rum, pineapple, bitter orange, and herbal flavors on the swallow.
instructions: Stir with ice, strain into an old fashioned glass with a large ice cube, and garnish with orange oil from a twist.

name: Stinger
description: A Stinger is a duo cocktail made by adding crème de menthe to brandy (although recipes vary). The cocktail's origins can be traced to the United States in the 1890s, and the beverage remained widely popular in America until the 1970s. It was seen as a drink of the upper class, and has had a somewhat wide cultural impact.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into chilled martini cocktail glass.

name: Stone’s Throw
description: What started as a thoughtful exercise about balance turned into a favorite cocktail: bright, grounded, herbal but refreshing, a cocktail that feels like it belongs in the roaring '20s—whether in a dimly lit bar or on a sun-drenched patio.
instructions:

name: Stork Club
description:
There is a number of cocktails, that came from various New York bars and clubs, which later became classics. Stork Club is one of those venues, that was known for its drinks, back in the day. However, some of those recipes slowly fell into obscurity, just like its signature Stork Club cocktail.

Base of the cocktail is London dry gin with its signature juniper notes supplemented by the gentle citrus and coriander undertones. Triple Sec adds sweet orange flavour, which is later reinforced by the healthy addition of fresh orange juice. A touch of lime juice brings some refreshing tartness to the mix, helping to bring back a little balance and give this cocktail a little pep in its step. Last, but not least a dash of Angostura bitters provides an extra kick of complexity while at the same time seasoning the cocktail.

All in all, Stork Club is a simple cocktail with a slightly unusual balance, due to mellow orange juice, but do not let that fool you, it is tasty – a true delight, especially for orange lovers. Even though it might be a little strange to our modern palate, it is a delicious way to travel back in time.
instructions:

name: Temperance Grapefruit Collins
description: The Temperance Grapefruit Collins is an extremely refreshing spirit-free interpretation of the gin-based cocktail of the same name.  As its star ingredient, the grapefruit serves as both the visual and flavor focal point of this simple cocktail.  In the absence of any alcohol, this combination of grapefruit juice, lime juice, and simple syrup is reminiscent of flavors found in the Paloma.  Similarly, as the name suggests, the Temperance Grapefruit Collins is served “tall” in the traditional Collins glass over ice cubes or clear ice spear and topped generously with club soda to give it some fizz.  When it comes to this cocktails preparation, I recommend shaking to both chill and incorporate ingredients; however, to avoid unnecessary explosions, be sure to refrain from adding club soda into the shaker and instead add directly to glassware.  Don’t forget to garnish your Temperance Grapefruit Collins with (you guessed it) a half-wheel of grapefruit.  But don’t take my word for it, make one and try it yourself!

The cocktail balances smoky Laphroaig scotch with bitter Campari and wildly herbal Chartreuse. It’s an unlikely blend with an unlikely ratio but wouldn’t you know, it’s perfectly balanced and delicious. It’s a sophisticated sipper, a gentleman’s nightcap, and features three ingredients easily found in most bars. Perhaps even found somewhere in the world, where puzzlers ponder, at the end of the road.

name: The Last Rainstorm
description:
Imagine: a view of a sandy beach shore peeking out between dense green vegetation and hovering tree canopies, the faint scent of salt from the sea suspended in the warm breeze, and that electrifying feeling of energy in the air right before a thunderstorm. You take a sip. Crisp. Cold. Tropical. Revitalizing. This is that drink.

Chartreuse is the dominant flavor, trailed by a comforting whisper of coconut aroma and the grassy & clean Copalli rum. When recreating, your choice of coconut rum will be pivotal in how the drink turns out; the best coconut rum I can recommend is the Hawaiian-made Koloa rum. More info on this rum can be found here but in short, it’s a fresh, natural, actual RUM that is scented with coconut and not a coconut LIQUEUR like many cloyingly sweet “coconut rums” tend to be.

This is dangerously easy-drinking for what it is, imbibe responsibly. Chartreuse = 55% Copalli rum = 42%. Koloa coconut rum = 40%.

name: The Tartan Cocktail
description: The Tartan Cocktail is a rich, layered winter drink that balances warmth and complexity. It starts with a foundation of single malt Scotch whisky, its oak and caramel notes softened by sweet vermouth’s cacao and citrus. Drambuie adds honeyed depth, while Amaro Ramazzotti introduces bitter-sweet orange and anise, all harmonized by a touch of Angostura bitters. Served stirred over a large ice cube, it evolves on the palate—perfect for cozy evenings.

name: The Warday’s

The Warday’s is an interesting booze filled cocktail with complex roots.

The cocktail borrows elements from two sources: Alaska (gin and yellow Chartreuse) and Manhattan (aged spirit, in this case represented by Calvados and sweet vermouth). By blending these ingredients together, a delicious booze filled cocktail is brought to life.

Notes of aged apples and pears are brought by the Calvados and then enriched by the botanicals of sweet vermouth. Gin contributes a healthy dose of juniper as well as a significant bite of alcohol. Final, modest, addition of yellow Chartreuse introduces a lot more herbal and botanical complexity as well as sweetness to the mix, nicely finishing the cocktail.

The Warday’s is a must try for seasoned cocktail enthusiasts. Rich, complex and delicious to the very last drop.

4. Garnish with orange wheel.

name: Thyme After Thyme
description: This dead simple gin cocktail from Charleston blends the slightly bitter and herbaceous notes of Cocchi Americano with tart grapefruit.
instructions:
1. Shake all of the ingredients together in a shaker with ice
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.

name: Ti’ Punch
description: This Caribbean favorite is the laid back cousin to the daiquiri. Kick your feet up with the 'Ti Punch.
instructions:
1. Slice half a lime into wedges
2. Muddle limes and syrup in a rocks glass
3. Add 2-3 pieces of ice and stir until melted

name: Ti’ Punch Highball
description: This stretches the classic Ti' Punch into a highball-like format with the addition of coconut water and tonic.
instructions:
1. In a highball glass, add the lime coin and muddle it to express the oils.
2. Add the sugar syrup, rum and 4 ice cubes and stir for a few seconds.
3. Add the coconut water and tonic water, then give one quick stir to integrate the ingredients.

lines.note: half-dollar-sized lime coin with some flesh on it

name: Tia Mia
description: This smoky twist on a Mai Tai combines Jamaican rum with mezcal, orange curaçao, orgeat, and fresh lime juice.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into a shaker with ice and shake until well chilled.
2. Strain into a large rocks glass over crushed or pebbled ice.
3. Garnish with lime wheel, mint sprig and orchid (optional).

name: Tiger’s Claw
description: Tiger’s Claw is an easy tropical cocktail recipe made with reposado tequila, pineapple, lime, coffee liqueur and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and shake with ice cubes.
2. Pour into a Collins glass.
3. Garnish with an orange half slice and mint sprig.

name: Tipperary
description: The Tipperary has been featured in old school cocktail books from 1916, 1922 and 1930. Two of the three call for equal parts but I've opted for an adapted recipe, lowering the Green Chartreuse, making for a more approachable version. Some recipes call for a dash or two of aromatic bitters and an orange twist.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into chilled martini cocktail glass.
garnish: Garnish with a slice of orange.

name: Tommy’s Margarita
description: Tommy's margarita was conceived in San Francisco in 1990. Although agave nectar was still expensive at the time, it is used to enhance the agave flavor of the cocktail instead of using triple sec to highlight the citrus flavor in the original Margarita recipe. In 2008, it became the first venue specific cocktail to be added to the IBA manual.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with ice.

name: Tonic Rickey
description: This simple non-alcoholic Tonic Rickey combines lime juice, simple syrup, tonic water, seltzer water, and Angostura bitters.
instructions:
1. In a lowball glass filled with ice, add the lime juice and simple syrup. Stir to combine.
2. Slowly stir in the tonic water and seltzer water.
3. Top with the bitters and serve.

name: Tonico di Corte
description: Put a little dinamismo in your G&T!
instructions:
1. Add tonic, Italicus, and gin to a highball glass filled with ice
2. Top with soda water and stir

name: Toronto
description:
This flavorful Toronto cocktail combines the depth and warmth of whiskey with the intrigue of herbal Fernet-Branca liqueur.

A recipe for the Fernet Cocktail calling for equal parts fernet and either cognac or rye whiskey was first printed in 1922 with the addendum that "this cocktail is much appreciated by the Canadians of Toronto."
instructions:
1. Combine the rye whiskey, Fernet-Branca, syrup and bitters in a cocktail mixing glass (or any other type of glass).
2. Fill the mixing glass with 1 handful ice and stir continuously for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a glass.
garnish: Garnish with an orange peel and serve.

name: Tradewinds Negroni
description: This is a spicy variation on the Negroni using equal parts sweet vermouth, Cointreau, and Angostura bitters. That's right: It's a lot of Angostura bitters.
instructions: Add sweet vermouth, Cointreau, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir until well chilled, about 25 seconds. Strain into an Old Fashioned glass with a large ice cube. Express orange oils from twist over drink, garnish with twist, and serve.

name: Trasatlántico Fizz
description: This bright and easy-drinking gin fizz combines winter citrus. The cocktail, created in 2013 in Buenos Aires, is a tribute to the immigration that came crossing the Atlantic by boat to the port of Buenos Aires.
instructions:
1. Combine all of the ingredients, except the club soda, in a shaker and shake hard for 10 seconds without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again for another 10 seconds.
3. Strain into a glass over ice and top with club soda.
4. Garnish.
garnish: Orange wedge and spritz of peated scotch

name: Treacle
description: This is an Old-Fashioned variation that has found lasting popularity. An inventive use of rum for the time. The preferred rum in this drink is Myers, with cheap, store brand apple juice, such as Mott’s, not the fresh-pressed apple juice young mixologists sometimes opted for, thinking they were improving the drink. More popular in the UK than in the U.S., where it is rarely seen. The drink’s exact place and year of birth are unknown.
instructions:
1. Build in a double rocks glass filled with ice.
2. Float cloudy apple juice on top.

name: Trinidad Sour
description: Unusually for a cocktail, it uses Angostura bitters as a base spirit rather than as a flavoring, the bitters being the single largest component of the drink in its IBA formulation.
instructions:
1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker
2. Shake well with ice
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Tropical Popsicle
description: A Japanese Whisky collins, with acidity, bitter notes and tropical flavors for a pop!
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients, except soda water, to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with cubed ice
4. Top with club soda

name: Tropical Storm
description: Passionfruit Syrup and dark rum shine in this daiquiri-hurricane hybrid.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker 
2. Add ice and shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled glass

name: Truly Scrumptious
description: Pear eau de vie and unaged South American grape brandy combine their fragrant forces in this luscious cocktail.
instructions: Shake all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass holding a single large ice cube. Garnish.

name: Tunnel
description: This recipe for the Tunnel is a Negroni-like drink. It combines gin, Campari and two types of vermouth.
instructions:
1. Stir all ingredients until chilled in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Strain into a coupe.

name: Turf Club
description: This Martini variation is a complex rendition of the classic made with absinthe and maraschino liqueur.
instructions:
1. Add the gin, dry vermouth, maraschino, absinthe, and bitters into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Tuxedo
description: Related to the martini, the Tuxedo has had many variations since its inception in the 1880s. The cocktail is named after the Tuxedo Club in Orange County, New York. Tuxedo Park, the planned community where the club was built, is itself a derivation of the Lenape word tucseto. The form of menswear by the same name originated at the same country club around the same time.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into chilled martini cocktail glass.
garnish: Garnish with cherry and lemon zest

name: Tuxedo No. 2
description: This variation on the Tuxedo cocktail recipe—a sherry-spiked Martini—dates to the turn of the 20th century and swaps sherry for dry vermouth.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients, except absinthe, in a mixing glass over cracked ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe rinsed or atomized with absinthe.
3. Express lemon twist, then use as garnish. Finish off with a brandied cherry.

name: Twelve Mile Limit
description: During the 18th century the US territorial waters were limited to 3 nautical miles. Throughout Prohibition it was legal to supply alcohol outside of these waters so parties hosted out at sea were common. This 3 mile limitation was later extended to 12 miles which led to the name inspiration for this Prohibition-era drink featuring grenadine.
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker, add all the ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe
4. Garnish with a twist of lemon

name: Ultima Palabra
description: Named after the direct Spanish translation of Last Word, hence the use of mezcal in place of the gin in a classic Last Word cocktail. Pineapple juice, another distinguishing feature of this riff on the classic, works brilliantly – adding a fruity sweetness and complexity.
instructions: 1. SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass

name: Ume Paloma
description: The Ume Paloma is a highball cocktail recipe combining blanco tequila, umeshu, pink grapefruit juice, lime juice and club soda.
instructions:
1. If using, rim a highball glass with sea salt.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
3. Add the club soda first, then the other ingredients.
4. Stir gently to blend.

name: Valkyrie
description: The Valkyrie is influenced by the Peralta, with its rye, Cynar, and grapefruit elements.
instructions: Stir with ice and strain into a rocks glass.
garnish: Twist a grapefruit peel over the top and discard

name: VE.N.TO
description: The Ve.n.to is one of the new additions to the IBA (International Bartender Association) cocktail list. And it is a truly unusual one, for it is the first-ever Grappa cocktail that made it into one of the lists of the IBA.
instructions:
1. Pour all ingredients into the shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled small tumbler glass filled with ice.

Notes:
If desired water can be replaced by chamomile infusion in the honey mix.
garnish: Garnish with lemon zest and white grapes.

name: Verte Chaud
description: An après-ski staple perfect for the chilly chartreuse fan
instructions:
1. Stir together hot water and shaved chocolate until combined
2. Add Chartreuse and top with wet cream

name: Vesper
description: The Vesper or Vesper Martini is a cocktail that was originally made of gin, vodka, and Kina Lillet. The formulations of its ingredients have changed since its original publication in print, and so some modern bartenders have created new versions which attempt to more closely mimic the original taste. The drink dates to 1953.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice cubes. Shake and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: Vieille Place
description: A twist on the classic Vieux Carré,  the Vieille Place is a balanced, yet spirit-forward, bittersweet aperitif. Created in Hassselt , Belgium, this drink incorporates Bourbon, Suze, Cognac, Dry Vermouth, Simple Syrup, a dash of Amaretto, aswell as both a dash of Peychard & Angostura Bitters.
instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass

name: Vieux Carrè
description: It originated in New Orleans. The name is French for "old square”, in reference to the city's French Quarter neighborhood.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
garnish: Garnish with orange zest and maraschino cherry.

name: Vitamin Parade
description: Fresh carrot and pineapple juices, citrus, ginger beer, and cinnamon syrup combine in this feel-good spirit-free drink.
instructions:
1. Combine the carrot juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry-shake with no ice for 15–20 seconds until foam forms.
3. Add ice and shake. Fine-strain into a fizz glass.
4. Top with ginger beer.
5. Express a lemon twist over cocktail then discard.

name: Ward Eight
description: The Ward Eight cocktail is a relative of the Whiskey Sour and thought to have been invented in Boston in 1898.
instructions: Shake ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass. Add an ice cube and a splash of sparkling water.

name: Wardman Park
instructions:
1. Stir with ice.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.

name: Washington's Mule
description: An autumnal and all-American version of the Moscow Mule.
instructions:
1. Combine syrup, brandy, lime juice, and bitters with ice in a cocktail shaker for a short shake. 
2. Strain over ice into a highball glass.
3. Top with soda water and stir.

name: Whiskey Apple Highball
description: It isn’t plausible to say one bar invented such a simple highball. But it was certainly perfected and popularized in Sydney, where whiskey was paired with freshly squeezed green apple juice, using a Breville juicer. The novel combination was a hit with the public immediately, partly due to its eye-catching, vivid-green color. The drink never really had a proper name and it wasn’t on the menu. People just knew it was available and ordered it. Soon bars across Sydney were serving the drink. Beginning in 2017, the highball hopped the Pacific and began showing up on menus at New York cocktail bars. That the Granny Smith apples are of good quality and are freshly juiced is vital to the success of the drink. The original whiskey used at the beginning was Jim Beam Rye, but many other ryes works just as well.
instructions:
1. Build in a highball filled with ice.
2. Stir.

name: Whiskey Business
description: The Whiskey Business cocktail recipe is a spicy riff on a Whiskey Sour featuring chile liqueur and cinnamon syrup.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a glass over a ice.
3. Garnish with lemon wheel dusted in ancho chile powder.
garnish: lemon wheel dusted in ancho chile powder

name: Whiskey Peach Smash
description: A riff on the OG Whiskey Smash, this Whiskey Peach Smash recipe adds fresh fruit and citrus to energize the classic formula.
instructions:
1. Muddle the fruit and lemon wedges with the Curaçao.
2. Add the mint leaves and the bourbon.
3. Shake well and strain into a double rocks glass filled with ice.
garnish: Garnish with a peach slice and a mint sprig

name: Whiskey Smash
description: A riff on the Mint Julep, the Whiskey Smash cocktail recipe features lemon and mint, making it a potent number dangerously easy to toss back.
instructions:
1. In a rocks glass, gently muddle mint with simple syrup to release oils.
2. Add lemon pieces and muddle to release juice.
3. Add crushed ice or small ice cubes and pour bourbon over.
4. Swizzle gently to mix.
5. Garnish with a mint spring and lemon wheel.

name: Whiskey Sour
description: The oldest historical mention of a whiskey sour was published in a Wisconsin newspaper in 1870. With egg white included, it is sometimes called a Boston Sour; when the whiskey used is a Scotch, it is called a Scotch Sour. With a few bar spoons of full-bodied red wine floated on top, it is often referred to as a New York Sour. It is shaken and served either straight up or over ice.
instructions:
1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake well.
3. Strain into cobbler glass.
4. If served “On the rocks”, strain ingredients into an old fashioned glass filled with ice.

NOTE:
If egg white is used shake little harder to release and incorporate the foam from the egg white.
garnish: Garnish with a half orange slice and maraschino cherry, optionally use orange zest.

name: Whisky Highball
description: Initially, the most common highball was made with Scotch whisky and carbonated water, known simply as a "Scotch and soda". The highball is said to have been brought to the U.S. in 1894 from England. Bartender Tip:Simple and refreshing cocktail with surprising complexity. One part whisky, two parts mixer, garnished with a lemon wedge and served over ice in a highball glass; the whisky highball is as simple as it is delicious
instructions:
1. Cut a lemon ready for garnishing and squeezing
2. Fill your highball with ice
3. Pour all the ingredients into your glass
4. Top up with soda water
5. Stir the drink gently together, mixing all the ingredients
6. Garnish with the lemon wedge

name: White Lady
description:
It was first created in 1919 in London and it was equal parts creme de menthe, triple sec and lemon juice. But four years later [1923], in Paris, France, the recipe had changed. The creme de menthe was swapped out for gin. Which, was a good move. But then, four years later [1927], a printed version of the White Lady no longer had gin. It went back to cremé de menthe, and it didn't have lemon juice. It had Brandy, and it was no longer equal parts. It was a completely different drink.

But then, 3 years later, in 1930, the White Lady was printed as gin, triple sec and lemon juice, only with an increased amount of gin to make a drier cocktail. Which is pretty much the cocktail we have today... and it's a great drink.

A few years after this drink became popular in London, a little egg white was suggested. But to this day, the egg white is considered optional.
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

name: White Mezcal Negroni
description: This White Negroni cocktail recipe swaps gin for mezcal and the expected Suze for Domaine La Bohème Gentiane Extra Bitter Aperitif.
instructions:
1. Combine in a mixing glass with ice and stir briefly for five seconds.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube or whatever ice you have.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist expressed over the drink, then discarded.

name: White Negroni
description: The White Negroni is a fabulous use of the gentian's powers, and a downright brilliant twist on a bonafide classic. All of the flavor components of a classic Negroni are present, but only the gin remains verbatim.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice and stir
2. Strain into a lowball glass

name: White Negroni (Corpse revived)
description:
We went nearly a century before a handful of rowdy boozehounds in NYC decided the Negroni needed more gin and less of everything else, but it took less than a decade for those same bartenders to tinker with the White Negroni. I think that was a mistake. 

While a classic Negroni can very easily handle an increase in gin to punch through the Campari and sweet red vermouth, there is far less sugar for the gin to fight in a White Negroni, rendering an increase of gin unnecessary and oftentimes detrimental. 

The best version of this cocktail then, in my opinion, adheres to the original Negroni format, stays true to the original White Negroni flavor profile, and improves upon the original.
instructions: Build in glass over ice

name: White Negroni Sbagliato
description: This White Negroni Sbagliato recipe mixes herbal Suze and bianco vermouth for a summer to fall spritz.
instructions:
1. Build over a large cube in a double Old-Fashioned glass.
2. Garnish with a long slice of cucumber and a twist of orange zest.

name: White Russian
description: Misleadingly, this sophisticated cocktail is not in fact Russian in origin, but gets its name from vodka being the base spirit. Traditionally a Black Russian, it becomes a White Russian with the addition of cream.
instructions:
1. Combine the vodka, coffee liqueur and ice cubes in a cocktail shaker
2. Shake well and strain into an ice-filled short tumbler
3. Lightly beat the single cream until just frothy and pour onto the drink over the back of a spoon, to help make it float

name: Wildest Redhead
description: This easy whiskey cocktail recipe combines blended Scotch whisky, allspice or pimento dram, Cherry Heering, lemon and honey syrup.
instructions:
1. Add the first four ingredients to a shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain over a large ice cube into a rocks glass.
3. Slowly pour the Cherry Heering over the ice so that it sinks to the bottom of the drink.

name: Willsour
instructions: Shake

name: Winterized Negroni
description: A half-teaspoon of Islay Scotch brings robust and malty flavors to the Negroni for a winterized take on the aperitivo classic.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a coupe glass.

name: Wisconsin Old Fashioned
description:
The Wisconsin Old Fashioned is the state’s variation on the classic Old Fashioned cocktail, with brandy and lemon lime soda. The typical Old Fashioned recipe uses bourbon mixed with a muddled sugar cube and bitters. So where did the brandy Old Fashioned come from?


Here’s the theory! A company of brothers debuted their Korbel brandy at the World’s Fair in 1893 in Chicago, which lots of Wisconsinites attended. A large percentage of Wisconsin at the time was German, and Germans preferred brandy over bourbon. Korbel brandy become a hit, and birthed this state’s funky variation on the classic cocktail. To this day, the drink is often served with Korbel brandy!


- Sweet: Lemon lime soda (like 7 Up or Sprite). This is the default option at bars.
- Sour: Sour mix or grapefruit soda (like Squirt).
- Press: 50/50 lemon lime soda and soda water (club soda)
- Soda: Soda water
instructions:
1. In a chilled old fashioned glass, muddle the sugar, bitters, orange wedge and cherry into a thick paste, careful not to overwork the orange peel.
2. Add brandy or Cognac and stir.
3. Fill glass with crushed ice and serve.

name: Wiz Fizz
description: In this fizzy cocktail recipe, gin, Cynar, lemon, and vanilla syrup act as a base, while egg white and heavy cream combine for a rich body.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass 1/5 full with root beer and set aside.
2. Combine the remaining ingredients, except the cream, in a mixing tin and dry shake without ice.
3. Add the cream and dry shake again.
4. Add ice and shake again for 30 to 40 seconds.
5. Strain the ice out of the shaker and dry shake once more for 1 minute.
6. Pour the contents of the shaker into the highball glass and allow to settle before adding a final topper.
garnish: Garnish with grated nutmeg and a straw.

name: Wray and Ting
description: Wray and Ting is a simple highball cocktail made with delicious overproof Jamaican rum and a refreshing grapefruit soda. Perfect for summer cookouts.
instructions:
1. Add ice to a collins glass.
2. Measure in the rum.
3. Top with Ting and garnish if you'd like.

name: Yellow
description: The Yellow is a cocktail recipe combining London dry gin, yellow Chartreuse, Suze and lemon juice in a Last Word-like drink.
instructions:
1. Combine the ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Double-strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
3. Express the lemon twists over the surface of the drink and discard.

name: Yellow Bird
instructions: Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, strain into chilled cocktail glass.

name: Your Mother’s Spritz
description: The white wine spritzer, popularized by "ladies who lunch" during the '50s, gets reimagined through a modern lens. While the original simply called for chilled white wine and club soda, this version is punchier, brighter, and far from basic, thanks to citrus-forward Italicus, with notes of bergamot and grapefruit that round it out beautifully.
instructions: 1. Add the ingredients, except the grapefruit soda, to a wine glass over ice. Top with the soda. Garnish.

name: Yuzu Negroni
description: In this take on the White Negroni, yuzu sake brightens up the bitter classic with citrus and floral notes.
instructions: 1. Add all the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice. Stir to chill and strain into the glass over a large ice cube. Express with a lemon peel and garnish.

name: Zombie
description: It first appeared in late 1934, invented in Hollywood. It was popularized on the East coast soon afterwards at the 1939 New York World's Fair.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into an electric blender with 170 grams of cracked ice.
2. With pulse bottom blend for a few seconds.
3. Serve in a tall tumbler glass.

Donn’s Mix: 2 parts of fresh yellow grapefruit and 1 part of cinnamon syrup

name: Zombie Apocalypse
description: A spooky, autumnal zombie riff that's perfect for a Halloween night! We added activated charcoal, which has hardly any taste, to produce the black color.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add a small amount of ice and shake until chilled
3. Strain over crushed ice into a chilled glass

name: Zombie Spritz
description: This low-ABV spritz tangles with the Zombie's famously layered build for a cocktail recipe that feels firmly rooted to both.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients, except the Cava rosé, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a goblet or tiki mug over crushed ice
3. Top with cava rosé.
garnish: dehydrated grapefruit slice, fresh mint, cocktail umbrella (optional)
